item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-27

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-27 01:36 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-27

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 正以极高吞吐量运行：过去 24 小时更新了 1,000 个条目（500 个 issue：400 个打开/活跃，100 个已关闭；500 个 PR：182 个打开，318 个已合并/关闭），其中很大一部分变更量由正在进行的内部性能/测试清理专项驱动（“deslop”、批量 d64x 测试移除、懒加载和 catalog 复用优化）。但是，没有发布任何版本，issue 跟踪器显示 P0“ux-release-blocker”报告持续累积——最集中于 Windows 更新/重启可靠性、SQLite/WAL 持久化和内存增长。社区注意力主要集中在少数高严重度、长期运行的讨论串上（最热 issue 已累积 139 条评论）。活动评估：维护者推进速度很高，但发布就绪度受制于一组尚未解决的 Windows/存储可靠性问题。

2. 发布

无。过去 24 小时没有新发布，“Latest Releases”信息流为空。鉴于多个打开的 P0 项带有 impact:ux-release-blocker 标签（尤其是 #143524、#160959、#170956、#166634），没有发布与发布列车被暂缓而非处于空闲状态的情况相符。没有迁移或破坏性变更说明需要报告。

3. 项目进展

318 个 PR 于今日被合并/关闭。值得注意的落地与推进：

  • 安全/UX： #185263（已关闭）——不再对常规 OAuth 访问令牌过期显示登录警告；Settings → Models 现在可区分令牌过期与不可用认证。
  • Web UI 修复： #185292（已关闭）——已保存的高亮文本 Side chat 评论无需二次提问即可提交；#184617（已关闭）——在 Control UI 上传前缩小过大的 JPEG 相机照片（修复 Android Chrome 附件失败）。
  • 性能： #185287（已关闭）——移除逐字段的 prompt-hook envelope 元组；#185249（已关闭）——移除未使用的插件根加载跟踪。
  • 进行中的高价值修复（打开）： #185250 阻止在 provider 认证冷却期间出现 prepared-runtime 重建风暴；#184293 将 compaction 的硬截止时间放到单调时钟上（修复时钟跳变导致的过早 compaction 失败）；#185293 防止长流式 HTML/JSX 回复在每个不完整标签上重新投影整个回复；#185238 修复 store SecretRef 认证令牌在 PostgreSQL 上导致 CLI Gateway 调用失败的问题；#185237 并发重建移植的内存索引以减少迁移停机时间；#183595 和 #184994/#184951 减少 Control UI 重载工作和过早的 chat-route 加载。
  • 表明缺陷已解决的已关闭 issue： #184315（operator.admin 因 operator.read 被拒——作用域语义）、#162899（Windows Control UI 托管更新在 validating 中冻结）、#89430（应用认证下 Google Chat 媒体投递 403）、#154517（sessions 删除/归档 not_found）、#172091（worker SQLite 事务在准入等待期间保持打开）、#150696（父级 yield 后 Codex-native 子活动）。

4. 社区热点

条目 状态 评论数 信号
#143524 SQLite WAL 增长到 1.4–2.8 GB，阻塞 Gateway 启动（Windows） 已关闭，P0 139 项目内最大的讨论串；Windows 上的存储层持久性是社区最大的单一关切。
#160959 Gateway 在捕获大型外部插件时阻塞数分钟（2026.9.6 回归） 打开，P0 57 插件代际捕获（#144252）引入事件循环饥饿；影响启动和运行时重新发布。
#159662 prepared-model-catalog.worker.js 无界泄漏约 4–5 GB/h 打开，P0 26 与 provider 无关，在冷重启后可复现；迫使小型主机频繁重启。
#170956 Windows 启动缓慢、插件关闭不干净、schtasks 权限错误 打开，P0 21 复合可靠性故障：重启/更新“只有在多次重试后才成功”。
#140010 Windows 睡眠/恢复后 WebSocket 重连中断 30–60 秒以上 打开，P1 16 笔记本电脑/移动主机的 UX；解冻恢复被繁忙的 Gateway 延后。
#182476 update repair 失败并出现 OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST 打开，P1 14 新出现（10 月 24 日），与更广泛的生命周期租约问题群一致。
#67419 Bootstrap 文件每轮重新注入，浪费 20–30% token 打开，P2，陈旧 14 最早的高可见度成本抱怨（创建于 4 月 15 日）。

潜在需求： (a) 在 Windows 上有一套可信的存储/检查点方案（WAL、完整性检查、事务、租约）；(b) 无论插件/模型目录规模如何，启动延迟可预测；(c) 在 8–16 GB 主机上内存有界；(d) 通过稳定的 prompt 前缀和非冗余上下文注入提升 token/成本效率。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

P0 / 发布阻塞（打开）

  • #160959 — Gateway 在大型外部插件上阻塞数分钟；自 2026.9.6 起回归。未标记修复 PR（no-new-fix-pr），需要维护者评审。
  • #159662 — prepared-model-catalog worker 中存在 4–5 GB/h 内存泄漏；未标记修复 PR。
  • #170956 — Windows 启动/关闭/schtasks 可靠性；修复形态明确，等待维护者。
  • #166634 — 崩溃恢复期间 checkpoint 过期，导致 agent 对 chat.history/models.list 永久处于 UNAVAILABLE；标记为 not-repro-on-main，需要复现。

P1（打开，值得注意）

  • #182476 update repair 期间出现 OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST（Windows）。
  • #183786 Windows beta 升级在查询已停止的前台 Gateway PID 时卡住。
  • #181432 2026.9.4 → 2026.10.5 后基线 RSS 从约 300 MB 回退到 1.89 GB（Linux ARM64），且 SQLite 事务保持 >1.5 秒。
  • #145203 openai-completions SSE 流挂起（48.5 分钟）后从未恢复；停滞看门狗因 stream_progress 饥饿。
  • #134993 2026.8.1 后，在大型 skill/agent 集群下，Gateway 在文件系统发现中占满一个 CPU 核。
  • #118885 启动时对多 GB 状态 DB 进行冗余的完整 PRAGMA integrity_check 遍历。
  • #172837 Codex nativeSubagentAssignments 在投递放弃后从未移除——每个新父线程都会重新固定/重新发送。
  • #177656 原生主机执行时出现 Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission（2026.10.5 上至少 28 次失败）。

P2 / 正确性与数据完整性

  • #166017 mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs 默认值未应用 → MCP 运行时从不被驱逐，broker 达到 256 子进程上限，所有 exec/MCP 启动失败。
  • #126906 拒绝 write 工具会静默禁用内存持久化，而 agent 报告成功。
  • #158070 预检 compaction 使进行中的投递失效（“tool caller authority is no longer active”）。
  • #178300 在 1 token 的 length 停止后出现虚假成功。
  • #129314、#151962 — 内部运行时字符串（“phantom user messages”）作为真实用户轮次浮现，未持久化到 transcript_events。
  • #146902、#143017 — 工具集频繁变动和前缀重写导致 prompt-cache 失效（一份报告测得 21.3M 缓存写入 token）。

修复 PR 可用性： 可形成修复/可排队的项包括 #168456（cron agentTurn 的 turn-key 断言导致 fallback 失败）和 #177094（系统通知镜像挤掉最后答案）。大多数 P0 存储/内存项明确标记为 clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr，即仍无人负责。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • 身份/安全： #162164 在 iOS/macOS 上可选启用个人身份，同时保留 Shared owner（活跃贡献映射，多个切片已合并）；#149024 主机级执行前授权守卫 + 空 allowlist 的 fail-closed 语义（需要安全评审）。
  • 资源感知调度： #161050 为 sessions_spawn/隔离 cron 运行提供内存压力感知准入——subagents.maxConcurrent 统计子进程数，而非 RSS（每个 claude-cli 子进程约 250–400 MB）。
  • 会话/UX 连续性： #112372 为 sessions_send 提供可选的、绑定来源的延迟完成（wakeOnReply）；#158800 在 /new 后浏览/分叉先前的频道聊天片段；#175826 Android 对等支持聊天内问题/原生审批。
  • 频道集成： #136271 为 Teams 文件上传提供动态 SharePoint 站点解析。

预测： 下一次发布（一旦切出）最可能以可靠性和性能为主，而不是新增表面功能——Control UI 重载/流式修复、编译/时钟正确性、PostgreSQL 认证令牌路径以及 catalog 复用优化。内存压力准入（#161050）和身份工作（#162164）看起来是下一周期最强的候选；两者仍受产品/安全决策约束。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • Windows 是主要痛点来源。 Windows 主机用户报告 WAL 增长到数 GB（#143524）、通过 schtasks 和生命周期租约发生的重启/更新失败（#170956、#182476、#183786、#170654）、更新器冻结（#162899，现已关闭）以及睡眠/恢复后重连中断（#140010）。情绪上是对重试密集恢复的挫败感（“只有在多次重试后才成功”）。
  • 小主机和多 agent 运维者触及资源上限。 4–5 GB/h 泄漏（#159662）、1.9 GB 基线 RSS（#181432）、MCP broker 在 256 个子进程时耗尽（#166017）以及单 CPU 核发现循环（#134993），使常开 Gateway 在普通硬件上不切实际。
  • 成本敏感度非常明确。 多份详细报告量化了 token 浪费：bootstrap 文件消耗 20–30% 上下文（#67419）、前缀重写产生 21.3M 缓存写入 token（#143017），以及工具集频繁变动破坏缓存复用（#146902）。
  • 对 agent 报告状态的信任因静默失败而受损：内存写入被拒绝时却报告成功（#126906）、截断后虚假成功（#178300）、微信/Slack 桥接中的幻影用户消息（#151962、#129314），以及崩溃恢复后 agent 永久不可用（#166634）。报告者技术水平很高，提供抓包记录和复现，并经常提交本地补丁——这是有投入的高级用户群体的强烈信号。

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告——个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态系统

时间窗口： 2026-10-27（24 小时社区摘要） · 项目： OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw、IronClaw

1. 生态系统概览

本样本中的五个项目已经收敛到一种共同架构——长期运行的网关/守护进程、通道适配器、工具/插件层、会话存储，以及记忆/检索后端——并且现在处于运行稳定性加固阶段，而不是功能扩展阶段：在窗口期内，所有项目都没有发布任何版本，尽管合计有 1,224 条 issue/PR 更新。竞争差异化已经从能力广度转向持久性、可诊断性和成本控制，缺陷主要集中在会话/准入语义、上下文压缩、记忆完整性和资源背压。生态系统呈现明显的双峰分布：OpenClaw 的体量约为任何同行的 20 倍（1,000 项 vs 100/72/52），而中等规模项目则显示贡献者供给持续超过评审能力。一个项目（IronClaw）处于休眠状态，这确认了该品类中的整合压力已经显现。

关键观察：

  • 除 OpenClaw 外，三个活跃同行项目合并了 127 个涉及 PR 中的 21 个（16.5%），而 OpenClaw 为 63.6%——OpenClaw 是唯一关闭速度快于积压速度的项目。
  • ZeroClaw 在 24 小时内关闭了 0 个 issue，却在一天内新开 8 个安全 issue。
  • 所有项目都表示，约束瓶颈是评审带宽，而不是接收量——OpenClaw（前 50 个中大多数带有 clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review）、Hermes（4 个 PR 已超过 60 天，其中一个因等待维护者点击 CI 批准而阻塞）、QwenPaw（17 个开启的 PR，其中包括若干 XL/XXXL）、ZeroClaw（5+ 个 needs-author-action，1 个 do-not-merge）。

3. OpenClaw 的位置

相对同行的优势

  • 社区规模与吞吐量： 24 小时 1,000 项（约为 QwenPaw 的 8 倍、Hermes 的 10 倍、ZeroClaw 的 19 倍）；最热帖有 139 条评论，而同行最高为 22 条。报告者会提交抓包和本地补丁——这是一个投入度很高的高级用户群体。
  • 基础设施完整度： 样本中唯一具备 PostgreSQL 后端选项、SecretRef 凭据抽象、状态租约、预置模型目录工作池，以及受单调时钟约束的压缩的项目。同行仍在修复单进程假设（Hermes #139818 远程恢复，QwenPaw #8279 线程耗尽）。
  • 发布纪律（反向）： 一个被暂停的发布列车比未暂停的发布列车是更强的信号——项目以自身 P0 为门禁，而不是带着 P0 发布（对比 Hermes，其 v0.22.5 稳定版带有一个未解决的准入冲突回归）。

技术路线差异 OpenClaw 的故障模式是基础设施层面的，而非逻辑层面的——多 GB 的 SQLite/WAL 增长（#143524）、执行 update repair 时状态租约丢失（#182476）、每小时 4–5 GB 的 worker 泄漏（#159662）、插件捕获期间事件循环饥饿（#160959）。这种画像是一个已经解决了 agent 逻辑、现在正为作为常开守护进程付出代价的系统的特征。同行项目在更靠栈底的位置失败（aiohttp 导入崩溃、线程池死锁、准入字面量），因为它们的运行时更简单。

社区规模对比 在每个互动指标上大约大一个数量级，但也带来相应负担：最高严重级别的条目明确无人负责——clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr 被附加到 #159662 和 #160959，而 #166634 被标记为 not-repro-on-main。体量已经超过了深度修复的人力供给。

6. 社区动能与成熟度

第 1 梯队——高速度、广覆盖（OpenClaw）。 PR 合并率 63.6%，每天 318 个落地，但很大一部分是内部专项搅动（“deslop”、批量删除测试、懒加载）。功能上最成熟；在 Windows 和 8–16 GB 主机上运行上最不稳定。快速迭代，发布受约束。

第 2 梯队——高互动、受评审约束（QwenPaw、Hermes）。 两者都呈现典型的中等规模特征：分流跟得上，深度修复跟不上。QwenPaw 能快速处理范围明确的报告（#8162 于 10 月 10 日提交，修复于 10 月 26 日合并；#8270 和 #4946 在本窗口关闭），但有 3 个严重且无修复 PR 的 bug，以及一个与隐私相关的 PR（#7835）自 9 月 17 日起未评审。Hermes 推进了 45 个 PR，但只合并了 5 个，同一天关闭了一个功能请求，并且对其三个最大稳定性风险（aiohttp 崩溃循环、webhook cron 死锁、准入问题簇）完全没有 PR。在表面能力上快速迭代，在核心上趋于稳定。 两者都展示了成熟度信号——生产环境 976 MB 历史数据库、Docker 部署、每日备份 cron。

第 3 梯队——安全加固，积压腐化风险（ZeroClaw）。 新进 23 个 issue，关闭 0 个；一天内提交 8 个安全 issue，且没有修复 PR；v0.9.0 的工作在未合并的父 PR 上堆叠了数层（#11234/#11230 基于 #11225）。运行上趋于稳定，但在以安全为主题的发布前正在累积未评审风险。

休眠（IronClaw）。

跨项目成熟度判断： 每个项目互动度最高的主题现在都是信任或可靠性主题帖，而不是能力公告——OpenClaw 的 139 条评论 WAL 主题帖、Hermes 的 22 条评论 session-resume 主题帖、QwenPaw 的 12 条评论插件契约主题帖、ZeroClaw 的上下文压缩问题簇。该品类已经从“它能做什么”跨到“我能不能让它一直跑着”。

7. 趋势信号

  1. 可靠性如今是发布门禁。 四个独立的 P0 ux-release-blocker 问题簇拦住了 OpenClaw 的发布列车；ZeroClaw 将安全工作标记为 release:v0.9.0/release-gate；Hermes 的稳定版 v0.22.5 发布时带有一个未解决的会话回归。含义：达到稳定版的延迟正成为竞争指标，而不仅仅是能力。

  2. 会话/租约/准入是新的难题。 这在三个网关型项目中都可见。具体建议：显式建模会话状态（owner、lease、TTL、generation），让唤醒幂等，用死信路径限制重试，并让上限可触达——Hermes #143720 显示一个 _MAX_COMPLETION_* 常量在当前活动路径中是死代码。

  3. 压缩必须被实现、移除或记录——绝不能形同虚设。 ZeroClaw 静默 no-op 的配置键（#10781）和破坏性 trim（#11711），加上 QwenPaw 的硬性压缩失败（#8312），使其成为生态系统中信任修复杠杆最高的单点。应交付 token 预算核算界面，而不仅仅是一项策略。

  4. 静默失败是跨项目第一号用户体验投诉（4/4 个活跃项目）。给 agent 开发者的两个具体模式：(a) 对于被拒绝、被截断或被丢弃的操作，绝不返回成功；(b) 让拒绝可被机器补救——原因 + 提示（#11983）——因为自主 agent 会在不透明错误上循环。

  5. 背压必须按消耗资源来设定维度。 四个项目各自限制错了计数器：限制子进程数而非 RSS（#161050）、限制线程池槽位而非事件循环进展（#145315）、限制默认 AnyIO 限制器而非任务数（#8279）、在缓冲后而非缓冲前限制响应大小（#12045）。

  6. 成本可观测性是采购标准。 量化浪费（bootstrap 重新注入消耗 20–30% 上下文；实测 21.3M 缓存写入 token）以及对按运行时设置思考级别（ZC #12054）和按操作为记忆写入选择模型（QP #7719）的需求。预计 token 核算仪表盘将成为基本门槛。

  7. 严格按规范实现的解析器会在真实环境中失败。 每个项目至少有一个 bug 由不符合规范的 OpenAI 兼容代理或网关引起。应构建带终止事件回退的宽容流解析器。

  8. 身份与最小权限正从可选转向发布门禁。 ZeroClaw 的 OIDC 栈、OpenClaw 的执行前授权防护和个人身份工作、Hermes 的 HITL 绕过修复都指向同一方向。能感知主体的工具作用域（而不只是角色检查）看起来将成为 2027 年自托管 agent 的基线要求。

  9. 插件供应链是新兴攻击面。 manifest/二进制生成不匹配（#11562）、插件生成捕获阻塞网关（#160959），以及未固定版本的第三方仪表盘脚本（#12053），是同一风险的三类不同表现。应将插件准入视为两阶段提交。

  10. Windows 与桌面端对齐仍是被服务不足的市场。 OpenClaw 最主要的痛点面是 Windows 存储/更新/睡眠恢复；QwenPaw 正积极投入 deb/AppImage 和 Wayland portal。对于“个人”助手而言——用户的实际机器就是部署目标——把 Windows 当作次级平台是一个持久的竞争空白。

给决策者的底线结论： OpenClaw 是参考实现，也是唯一关闭速度快于积压速度的项目——但它被一个无人负责的 Windows/存储 P0 问题簇阻塞，其发布就绪度是生态系统近期最明确的风险（也是机会）。QwenPaw 是管理最好的中等规模项目，也是桌面/CJK 用例最强押注。Hermes 拥有最丰富的编排表面和最弱的会话层。ZeroClaw 做出了正确的长期架构押注（身份、完整性、主权），但目前受限于评审吞吐量。在架构上，生态系统已经趋同；未来两个季度的差异化因素将是：谁最先把这种趋同转化为可信赖、有界、可诊断的常开行为。

1. 今日概览

活跃度仍然很高：过去 24 小时内涉及 50 个 issue 和 50 个 PR，但合并比例偏低——45 个 PR 仍处于打开状态，仅 5 个已合并/关闭，且未发布任何版本。issue 流由单一架构主题主导：会话身份、唤醒/准入与恢复语义，横跨网关、cron、Discord 和桌面客户端；其中四份独立报告涉及 admission_conflict 拒绝循环，有一份一天内达到 2,641 次。第二组问题涉及网关与 CLI 之间的规范 API 契约不匹配（data.fields 对 data.field、继承的 HERMES_SESSION_SOURCE 标签），表明这是模式治理缺口，而非孤立缺陷。积极的一面是，维护者当天关闭了一个功能请求（#145313），三项可见 PR 已合入，社区也在提交内容充实、复现良好的报告以及自己的修复 PR。整体健康度：参与度高、分诊吞吐量高，但会话/网关层的稳定性债务不断累积，PR 队列存在评审瓶颈。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

今日窗口内没有 issue 被标记为 P1，但若干 P2 项具有崩溃循环或消息丢失的影响范围。

严重（崩溃循环 / 死锁 / 数据面停滞）

  1. #144560 (P2, gateway/webhook) — 当 aiohttp 缺失时，网关会陷入崩溃循环，因为 -> web.Response 注解会在导入时求值（66 处，ruff UP037）。降级环境变成硬失败，而不是优雅跳过适配器。未见修复 PR。
  2. #145315 (P2，今日新增) — Webhook cron_job 路由在同时触发的运行数达到默认线程池线程数后，会使整个网关死锁：asyncio.to_thread 占用一个线程，而该线程随后无限等待所属事件循环。干净、可复现、架构性问题。未见修复 PR。
  3. #145292 (P2, MCP) — 永不完成的传输拆除会让 _serve_session 的运行循环卡住；MCP 工具永远不会恢复。需要在 ClientSession/transport_cm 退出时设置超时。
  4. #145308 (P2, gateway/sessions) — 在由 message_agent 启动的回合中，clarify 从不渲染，却持有会话租约，导致 restart --yes 等待它而挂起。

  2. #139818 (P2, sweeper:risk-session-state) — 一旦托管进程消失，远程后端桌面会话的 session.resume → not_found。

7. 用户反馈摘要

按数量排序的痛点：

  1. 静默、无帮助的失败。 三份独立报告描述了相同体验：一次变更被拒绝，UI 显示通用文案，而重试永不停止。来自 #145286：一个精确指明出错字段的 invalid_params 却显示为*“Hermes 无法启动模型连接。”* 来自 #141878：插件激活时的 401 被静默丢弃。来自 #145298：permission_denied 看起来像操作系统缺陷，因为拖放入口仍保持启用。用户明确要求错误文案保真，而不仅仅是正确性。
  2. 没有上限的重试风暴。 #145261（2,641 次拒绝/天）、#143720（尝试次数上限从未触发）、#142461。填满日志、消耗配额，并掩盖真实失败。
  3. 部署形态假设。 自托管者运行远程 hermes serve + 桌面客户端 + 多个 profile（#139818、#145261），外加 ACP 查看器（#144438），以及没有 systemd 的 WSL2（#119805）。若干缺陷只在这些“常开/多路复用”拓扑中出现，说明顺利路径是单进程本地运行。
  4. 对捆绑内容的信任。 #145276/#145304/#145306 这一组——均由同一位报告者在检查 skills/ 引用时提交——表明用户会阅读并运行捆绑示例，而错误示例（0/0 除法、git checkout -- 破坏工作）会被视为产品缺陷，其中一个还打了 area/i18n 标签。
  5. 合法自动化被当作敌意行为。 #105758：一个旨在防止自我终止的生命周期守卫阻止了无害的 Node.js CLI。needs-decision 标签表明这是一个策略问题，而它现已搁置 7 周、有 15 条评论。

满意信号： 报告篇幅长、埋点充分（日志计数、提交、复现），且常包含根因分析——这表明用户群体投入且技术成熟。多位用户提交了自己的修复 PR（100yenadmin、unsupportedpastels、arimu1、teknium1），且有一个 issue 当天解决。

7. 用户反馈摘要

按数量排序的痛点：

  • 提供方/网关兼容性（呼声最高）： 不符合规范的 OpenAI Responses 流（#8162）、Volcengine glm-5.3-flash 拒绝两个 thinking 禁用参数（#8417）。用户运行异构的国内外网关；严格遵循规范反而会使其失效。
  • 长期记忆信任： 静默批次丢弃（#8040）、重排器校验薄弱（#8276）、长时间运行部署中的 AnyIO 耗尽（#8279）。
  • 上下文管理： 压缩直接失败（#8312、#8417）——用户遭遇硬性任务中断，而非优雅降级。
  • 本地化/数据完整性： Windows ZIP 乱码（#8270）、CRLF 重新编码（#8415）——两者都尤其影响 CJK 与混合编码工作流。
  • 升级回归： 升级后邮件监控认证中断（#8425）——配置迁移未处理已存在的完整地址 name 字段。

满意信号： 对于范围明确的报告，处理速度确实很快——#8162 于 10 月 10 日提交，其修复 PR 同日落地，并于 10 月 26 日关闭；#8270 和 #4946 也在本窗口关闭。用户显然正将 QwenPaw 作为生产基础设施部署（976 MB 历史数据库、Docker 部署、每日备份 cron），这是强烈的成熟度信号。

不满意信号： “零日志”挂起（#8435）、误导性的“unexpected error”提示（#8276），以及有损编辑却报告“Successfully replaced text”（#8415）。用户的抱怨与其说是缺少功能，不如说是 agent 失败时的可诊断性。

10 #12053 仪表盘源上未固定版本的第三方脚本 S2 / 安全 仪表盘源上的供应链 XSS 无修复 PR
11 #11562 插件清单/组件代际不匹配 S2 / risk:high 在已被替换代际的清单下运行组件 修复 PR #12040 已打开
12 #11711 历史裁剪永久删除较早轮次 S2 长会话中的静默数据丢失 无修复 PR
13 #10921 Qdrant 有时间边界的召回遗漏符合条件的结果 S2 召回质量下降 无修复 PR
14 #12043 glob_search 丢弃已授权的跨工作区匹配；在只读根下拒绝绝对模式 S2 工具在两种方向上误报可见性 无修复 PR
15 #12021 配置保存按钮在 Save all 后仍保持高亮 S3 UI 状态混乱 修复 PR #12039 已打开
16 #11825 codex_cli 测试清空进程 PATH，破坏并行 cargo test S3 CI/测试隔离不稳定 无修复 PR

评估： 安全集群异常密集，似乎是单个评审者的一轮审计（#12046–#12053，全部为 S2，全部零评论，全部于 2026-10-26 提交）。大多数尚无配套修复 PR，这是进入 v0.9.0 的主要稳定性风险。只有 #11562 和 #12021 有正在进行的修复。

5. 功能请求与路线图信号

请求 链接 信号
用于记忆召回的可选外部重排序阶段（/v1/rerank，默认关闭，失败时开放到本地路径） #12022 记忆质量可扩展性；低风险，可能在 v0.9.x
对原生 OpenAI reasoning 遵循每个运行时配置档的思考级别 #12054 多 agent、单提供商差异化；范围较小
根据配置的仪表盘源而非 Host 头验证 OIDC redirect_uri #12048 安全增强，与 #11965 栈配套
Gitea/Forgejo 与 GitHub forge 渠道对齐 #12041 自托管/主权部署需求
统一文件接收/解析/投影/投递（RFC #9488 后跟踪器） #11013 多渠道文件处理架构
实现或移除失效的上下文配置键 #10781 与 #10780 相关的清理

对下几个版本的预测：

  • v0.8.7（即将到来）： 插件准入修复（#11562/#12040）、翻译目录固定（#12019）。低风险维护版本。
  • v0.9.0： OIDC 仪表盘登录 + 带作用域的仪表盘聊天（#11965、#11986、#11968、#11963），以及 RPC/身份访问加固（#11289、#11326、#11234、#11230）——均明确标记为 release:v0.9.0/release-gate。八个新的安全 issue 很可能被并入这轮加固。
  • v0.9.0 之后： 一次上下文管理重构，处理 #10780/#10781/#11711，以及 Goal V1 监督提案（#11880/#11882）在其评审门通过后——目前标记为“FAIL”，因此不是近期事项。

6. 用户反馈摘要

  • 配置信任侵蚀。 用户设置 context_compression.*、history_pruning.keep_recent、collapse_tool_results 期望节省 token；但什么都没发生（#10781）。结合 #10780 和 #11711，这是最强烈的不满信号：功能看似存在，但要么失效，要么具有破坏性。
  • 长会话中的数据丢失焦虑。 #11711（裁剪重写转录，删除较早轮次）是对任何运行持久网关对话的人来说最用户可见的正确性风险。
  • 记忆质量差距。 #10921（有时间边界的召回遗漏符合条件的结果）和 #12022（外部重排序请求）表明用户正推动记忆从“能用”走向“可预测且可调”。
  • UI 打磨很重要。 #12021 表明 Web 仪表盘的小状态缺陷会被注意到并及时提交（一天内出现修复 PR），说明仪表盘用户群体参与度较高。
  • 渠道可靠性。 Telegram 用户遇到 429 处理不当（#11651）以及终端语音转录重试循环阻塞长轮询偏移量（#11601）——两者都有修复 PR，但都标记为 needs-author-action。
  • Agent 自我纠正摩擦。 #11983 认为仅给出“Command not allowed by security policy”消息会导致 agent 重试变体而不是修复问题；修复方案增加原因 + 提示。这是一个反复出现的主题：安全拒绝必须能向模型解释。
  • 外部验证。 #12042 是一份主动的 Hlido 评审，给 ZeroClaw 打分 79/100，并开放回复权。值得注意的是，这是对项目自主性/安全姿态的第三方审视；也表明面向 agent 的评审目录现在正将该项目作为目标。
  • 贡献者体验。 #11825（测试修改进程范围的 PATH，破坏并行 cargo test）对贡献者来说是一个小而真实的摩擦点。

7. 积压事项关注

需要维护者关注的事项：打开时间最长、严重性最高或带有明确阻塞标签：

时长 事项 为何需要关注
50 天 #10673 P1/S1 自 Sep 7 起打开的传输一致性缺陷，4 条评论，无修复 PR——窗口期内最古老的未解决 P1
46 天 #10780 P1 自 Sep 11 起为 status:in-progress，没有实现 PR；阻塞 #10781 清理和 #11711 正确性
40 天 #10921 记忆召回正确性，4 条评论，看不到负责人
37 天 #11013 已接受 RFC #9488 的实现跟踪器；没有里程碑分配的跟踪器会腐烂
28 天 #11234 和 #11230 priority:p1、release-gate、size:XL，叠加在未合并的 #11225 上——评审链是瓶颈
27 天 #11289 带有 do-not-merge，同时为 priority:p2/risk:high；需要一个决定，而不仅仅是一个标签
26 天 #11326 针对受限主体读取持久化日志的 release-gate 修复——与安全相关且停滞
20/17 天 #11601、#11651 两者均为 needs-author-action；Telegram 可靠性修复闲置
8 天 #11847 size:XL XMPP 渠道——大面积，需要评审者带宽，以免与 master 偏离

流程观察： 在整个样本中，5+ 个 PR 带有 needs-author-action，1 个带有 do-not-merge，而 24 小时内关闭了 0 个 issue 且仅关闭 1 个 PR。项目当前的健康约束是评审/合并吞吐和作者跟进，而不是贡献量——值得在下一次维护者同步中提出，尤其是单日落地了 8 个 issue 的安全审计，且标记为 v0.9.0 的工作已经堆叠了数个 PR 之深。

数据说明：数据集列出 29 个有更新的 PR 中的 20 个；唯一合并/关闭的 PR 不在其中，且 PR 评论数提供为 undefined，因此 PR 的“热度”是从标签（风险、规模、发布标签）推断的，而不是参与度。所有 issue 评论数均按样本中报告。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-27

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-27 01:36 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-27

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw is operating at very high throughput: 1,000 items were updated in the last 24 hours (500 issues: 400 open/active, 100 closed; 500 PRs: 182 open, 318 merged/closed), with a large share of churn driven by an ongoing internal performance/test-cleanup campaign ("deslop", batch d64x test removals, lazy-loading and catalog-reuse optimizations). However, zero releases were cut, and the issue tracker shows an accumulation of P0 "ux-release-blocker" reports — most concentrated in Windows update/restart reliability, SQLite/WAL persistence, and memory growth. Community attention is dominated by a small number of high-severity, long-running threads (the top issue accumulated 139 comments). Activity assessment: high maintainer velocity, but release readiness is constrained by an unresolved Windows/storage reliability cluster.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24 hours and the "Latest Releases" feed is empty. Given multiple open P0 items tagged impact:ux-release-blocker (notably #143524, #160959, #170956, #166634), the absence of a release is consistent with a held release train rather than an idle one. No migration or breaking-change notes to report.

3. Project Progress

318 PRs were merged/closed today. Notable landings and advances:

  • Security/UX: #185263 (closed) — stop surfacing sign-in warnings for routine OAuth access-token expiry; Settings → Models now distinguishes expiry from unusable auth.
  • Web UI fixes: #185292 (closed) — saved highlighted-text Side chat comments can be submitted without a second question; #184617 (closed) — resize oversized JPEG camera photos before Control UI upload (Android Chrome attach failure).
  • Performance: #185287 (closed) — remove per-field prompt-hook envelope tuples; #185249 (closed) — drop unused plugin root load tracking.
  • In-flight high-value fixes (open): #185250 stops prepared-runtime rebuild storms during provider auth cooldowns; #184293 puts compaction's hard deadline on the monotonic clock (fixes clock-jump-induced premature compaction failure); #185293 prevents long streamed HTML/JSX replies from re-projecting the entire reply on every partial tag; #185238 fixes store SecretRef auth tokens breaking CLI Gateway calls on PostgreSQL; #185237 rebuilds ported memory indexes concurrently to cut migration downtime; #183595 and #184994/#184951 reduce Control UI reload work and premature chat-route loading.
  • Closed issues indicating resolved defects: #184315 (operator.admin rejected for operator.read — scope semantics), #162899 (Windows Control UI managed update freeze in validating), #89430 (Google Chat media delivery 403 under app auth), #154517 (sessions delete/archive not_found), #172091 (worker SQLite transaction held open behind admission wait), #150696 (Codex-native child activity after parent yield).

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Status Comments Signal
#143524 SQLite WAL grows to 1.4–2.8 GB, blocks gateway startup (Windows) CLOSED, P0 139 Largest thread in the project; storage-layer durability on Windows is the single biggest community concern.
#160959 Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) OPEN, P0 57 Event-loop starvation introduced by plugin generation capture (#144252); affects startup and runtime republish.
#159662 prepared-model-catalog.worker.js unbounded leak ~4–5 GB/h OPEN, P0 26 Provider-agnostic, reproduced on cold reboot; forces frequent restarts on small hosts.
#170956 Windows slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, schtasks permission error OPEN, P0 21 Compound reliability failure: restarts/updates "only after many retries".
#140010 Sleep/resume on Windows breaks WebSocket reconnect for 30–60s+ OPEN, P1 16 Laptop/mobile-host UX; thaw recovery defers behind busy gateway.
#182476 update repair fails with OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST OPEN, P1 14 New (Oct 24) and consistent with the broader lifecycle-lease cluster.
#67419 Bootstrap files re-injected every turn, wasting 20–30% tokens OPEN, P2, stale 14 Oldest high-visibility cost complaint (created Apr 15).

Underlying needs: (a) a trustworthy storage/checkpointing story on Windows (WAL, integrity checks, transactions, leases); (b) predictable startup latency regardless of plugin/model-catalog size; (c) bounded memory on 8–16 GB hosts; (d) token/cost efficiency via stable prompt prefixes and non-redundant context injection.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / release-blocking (open)

  • #160959 — Gateway blocks for minutes on large external plugins; regression from 2026.9.6. No fix PR flagged (no-new-fix-pr), needs maintainer review.
  • #159662 — 4–5 GB/h memory leak in prepared-model-catalog worker; no fix PR flagged.
  • #170956 — Windows startup/shutdown/schtasks reliability; fix shape clear, awaiting maintainer.
  • #166634 — checkpoint expiry during crash recovery leaves an agent permanently UNAVAILABLE for chat.history/models.list; marked not-repro-on-main, needs repro.

P1 (open, notable)

  • #182476 OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST during update repair (Windows).
  • #183786 Windows beta upgrade stalls querying a stopped foreground Gateway PID.
  • #181432 Baseline RSS regressed ~300 MB → 1.89 GB after 2026.9.4 → 2026.10.5 (Linux ARM64), with SQLite transaction holds >1.5 s.
  • #145203 Hung openai-completions SSE stream (48.5 min) never recovered; stall watchdog starved by stream_progress.
  • #134993 Gateway pegs one CPU core in filesystem discovery after 2026.8.1 with large skill/agent fleets.
  • #118885 Redundant full PRAGMA integrity_check passes over multi-GB state DB at startup.
  • #172837 Codex nativeSubagentAssignments never removed after delivery gives up — re-pinned/re-sent each new parent thread.
  • #177656 Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission on native host exec (≥28 failures on 2026.10.5).

P2 / correctness and data-integrity

  • #166017 mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs default not applied → MCP runtimes never evicted, broker hits 256-child cap and all exec/MCP starts fail.
  • #126906 Denying write tool silently disables memory persistence while the agent reports success.
  • #158070 Preflight compaction voids in-flight delivery ("tool caller authority is no longer active").
  • #178300 False success after a 1-token length stop.
  • #129314, #151962 — internal runtime strings ("phantom user messages") surfacing as real user turns, not persisted to transcript_events.
  • #146902, #143017 — prompt-cache defeat via tool-set churn and prefix rewrites (21.3M cache-write tokens measured in one report).

Fix-PR availability: Fix-shaped/queueable items include #168456 (fallback dies on turn-key assertion for cron agentTurn) and #177094 (system-notice mirror displaces last answer). Most P0 storage/memory items are explicitly tagged clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr, i.e., still unowned.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Identity/security: #162164 opt-in personal identity on iOS/macOS while preserving Shared owner (active contribution map, multiple merged slices); #149024 host-wide pre-execution authorization guard + fail-closed empty allowlist semantics (security review needed).
  • Resource-aware scheduling: #161050 memory-pressure-aware admission for sessions_spawn/isolated cron runs — subagents.maxConcurrent counts children, not RSS (~250–400 MB per claude-cli child).
  • Session/UX continuity: #112372 opt-in origin-bound deferred completion (wakeOnReply) for sessions_send; #158800 browse/fork prior channel-chat segments after /new; #175826 Android parity for in-chat questions/native approvals.
  • Channel integrations: #136271 dynamic SharePoint site resolution for Teams file uploads.

Prediction: the next release (when cut) is most likely dominated by reliability and performance rather than new surface area — Control UI reload/streaming fixes, compilation/clock correctness, PostgreSQL auth-token path, and catalog-reuse optimizations. Memory-pressure admission (#161050) and identity work (#162164) look like the strongest candidates for the following cycle; both are still gated on product/security decisions.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Windows is the dominant pain surface. Windows-host users report WAL growth to multi-GB (#143524), restart/update failures via schtasks and lifecycle leases (#170956, #182476, #183786, #170654), updater freezes (#162899, now closed), and broken sleep/resume reconnect (#140010). Sentiment is frustration with retry-heavy recovery ("only after many retries").
  • Small-host and multi-agent operators hit resource ceilings. 4–5 GB/h leaks (#159662), 1.9 GB baseline RSS (#181432), MCP broker exhaustion at 256 children (#166017), and one-CPU-core discovery loops (#134993) make always-on gateways impractical on modest hardware.
  • Cost sensitivity is explicit. Multiple detailed reports quantify token waste: 20–30% of context consumed by bootstrap files (#67419), 21.3M cache-write tokens from prefix rewrites (#143017), and tool-set churn breaking cache reuse (#146902).
  • Trust in agent-reported state is eroded by silent failures: memory writes reported successful when denied (#126906), false success after truncation (#178300), phantom user messages in WeChat/Slack bridges (#151962, #129314), and agents left permanently unavailable after crash recovery (#166634). Reporters are highly technical, provide wire captures and reproductions, and frequently ship local patches — a strong signal of an invested power-user base.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived or low-attention items needing maintainer decisions:

  • #67419 (Apr 15) — context bloat / bootstrap re-injection; 14 comments, 2 👍, tagged needs-product-decision. Highest-leverage cost fix still undecided.
  • #118885 (Aug 3) — redundant startup integrity checks on multi-GB DBs; P1, needs-product-decision, bulk-filed.
  • #129314 (Aug 25) — internal context leaking as standalone turns; stale, needs-info, session-state.
  • #114414 — dated TODO sweep listing overdue CI/auth and workflow cleanup; a recurring hygiene debt marker.
  • #136271 and #112372 — both have open linked PRs but remain stalled on product decisions.
  • PR side: #144685 (macOS approval-panel dismissal, created Sep 11) is still in needs proof; #183595 is explicitly "ready for maintainer review; stop before merge" with one unresolved candidate-only terminal test failure — a candidate for maintainer time.
  • clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review is attached to a large fraction of the top-50 issues, indicating review bandwidth, not issue intake, is the current bottleneck.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Window: 2026-10-27 (24h community digests) · Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, IronClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The five projects in this sample have converged on a common architecture — a long-lived gateway/daemon, channel adapters, a tool/plugin layer, a session store, and a memory/retrieval backend — and are now in an operational hardening phase rather than a feature-expansion phase: not a single release was cut across any project in the window, despite 1,224 combined issue/PR updates. Competitive differentiation has shifted from capability breadth to durability, diagnosability, and cost control, with the bug mass concentrated in session/admission semantics, context compaction, memory integrity, and resource backpressure. The ecosystem is sharply bimodal: OpenClaw operates at ~20× the volume of any peer (1,000 items vs 100/72/52), while the mid-sized projects show contributor supply consistently exceeding review capacity. One project (IronClaw) is dormant, confirming that consolidation pressure is already active in this category.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (open/closed) PRs (open/merged) Merge/close rate Release status Health score
OpenClaw 500 (400 / 100) 500 (182 / 318) 63.6% PR · 20% issue None — train held by 4 open P0 ux-release-blockers 7.0 / 10
QwenPaw 24 (17 / 7) 48 (33 / 15) 31.3% PR · 29% issue None — 2.2.3b1 beta in flight 6.5 / 10
Hermes Agent 50 (split n/d) 50 (45 / 5) 10.0% PR None — latest stable v0.22.5 carries regressions 5.0 / 10
ZeroClaw 23 (23 / 0) 29 (28 / 1) 3.4% PR · 0% issue None — v0.8.7 RC prep, v0.9.0 work stacked 3.5 / 10
IronClaw 0 0 — None Dormant

Health score rubric (composite, /10): closure throughput 30% · release readiness / P0 burden 30% · review responsiveness 20% · engagement quality 20%. Scores are comparative within this sample, not absolute quality judgments.

Key observations:

  • Excluding OpenClaw, the three active peers merged 21 of 127 touched PRs (16.5%) vs OpenClaw's 63.6% — OpenClaw is the only project closing faster than it accumulates.
  • ZeroClaw closed zero issues in 24h while opening 8 security issues in a single day.
  • All projects report review bandwidth, not intake, as the binding constraint — OpenClaw (clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review on most of the top 50), Hermes (4 PRs >60 days old, one blocked on a maintainer CI approval click), QwenPaw (17 open PRs incl. several XL/XXXL), ZeroClaw (5+ needs-author-action, 1 do-not-merge).

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs peers

  • Scale of community and throughput: 1,000 items/24h (~8× QwenPaw, ~10× Hermes, ~19× ZeroClaw); the top thread has 139 comments vs a peer maximum of 22. Reporters ship wire captures and local patches — an invested power-user base.
  • Infrastructure completeness: the only project in the sample with a PostgreSQL backend option, SecretRef credential abstraction, state leases, prepared-model-catalog worker pools, and monotonic-clock-bounded compaction. Peers are still fixing single-process assumptions (Hermes #139818 remote resume, QwenPaw #8279 thread exhaustion).
  • Release discipline (inverted): a held release train is a stronger signal than an unheld one — the project is gated on its own P0s rather than shipping through them (contrast Hermes, where v0.22.5 stable carries an unresolved admission-conflict regression).

Technical approach differences OpenClaw's failure modes are infrastructural rather than logical — multi-GB SQLite/WAL growth (#143524), state-lease loss on update repair (#182476), 4–5 GB/h worker leaks (#159662), event-loop starvation during plugin capture (#160959). That profile is the signature of a system that has already solved the agent logic and is now paying the tax on being an always-on daemon. Peer projects fail earlier in the stack (aiohttp import crash, thread-pool deadlock, admission literals) because their runtimes are simpler.

Community size comparison Roughly an order of magnitude larger on every engagement metric, but with a corresponding liability: the highest-severity items are explicitly unowned — clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr is attached to #159662 and #160959, and #166634 is tagged not-repro-on-main. Volume has outrun deep-fix labor.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Requirement Projects Specific needs
Context/token economics & non-destructive compaction OpenClaw, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw, Hermes Bootstrap re-injection costing 20–30% of context (OC #67419); 21.3M cache-write tokens from prefix rewrites (OC #143017); context_compression.* config keys silently inert (ZC #10780/#10781); trim permanently deletes turns (ZC #11711); compaction cannot fit a request at all (QP #8312, #8417)
Session identity, admission & wake semantics Hermes, OpenClaw, ZeroClaw admission_conflict refusal loops at 2,641/day with attempt caps that never fire (Hermes #145261, #143720, #142461); checkpoint expiry leaving an agent permanently UNAVAILABLE (OC #166634); failed ACP turns not persisted on the daemon RPC path (ZC #10673)
Durable persistence & data integrity All four active WAL/integrity-check cost and transaction holds (OC #143524, #118885, #172091); remote session.resume → not_found (Hermes #139818); silent embedding batch drops (QP #8040); lossy CRLF/encoding rewrite reported as success (QP #8415); plugin manifest/binary generation mismatch (ZC #11562)
Silent-failure elimination / diagnosability All four active "126/126 processed" while dropping a batch (QP #8040); zero-log indefinite hangs (QP #8435); data.fields vs data.field turning a precise refusal into "couldn't start the model connection" (Hermes #145286); memory write denied but reported successful (OC #126906); bare "Command not allowed by security policy" causing agent retry loops (ZC #11983)
Resource-bounded concurrency & backpressure All four active Concurrency capped on the wrong dimension — child count instead of RSS (OC #161050, #166017 256-child cap); 1.89 GB baseline RSS (OC #181432); AnyIO thread-limiter exhaustion (QP #8279); webhook cron deadlock at thread-pool size (Hermes #145315); unbounded response buffering (ZC #12045)
Provider/proxy compatibility tolerance QwenPaw, Hermes, OpenClaw Non-conforming OpenAI Responses streams (QP #8162); SGLang misclassified as Ollama, missing Gemini thought_signature, missing x-api-key path (Hermes #145309, #104345, #145275); auth-cooldown rebuild storms (OC #185250)
Identity & least-privilege as release gate ZeroClaw, OpenClaw, Hermes 8-issue OIDC/tool-scoping sweep incl. SOP privilege escalation, XFF limiter bypass, callback CSRF (ZC #12046–#12053); host-wide pre-exec authz with fail-closed defaults (OC #149024); A2A no-token-mode hardening, HITL approval bypass (Hermes #145310, #131461)
Plugin/channel contract depth QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, Hermes Semantic token theming instead of colorPrimary (QP #8071); nested skill dirs, channels-as-subprocesses (QP #8178, #8187); plugin generation integrity (ZC #11562); plugin activation 401 swallowed (Hermes #141878)

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Primary form factor Gateway daemon + Control UI (web), Windows-heavy install base Gateway + remote hermes serve + desktop client + ACP editor integrations (Zed/VS Code/JetBrains/Obsidian) Desktop application (Console, PawApp SDK, deb/AppImage, Finder/Explorer integration, Chrome native messaging) Rust daemon + RPC + web dashboard
Target user Power users / small teams running always-on multi-agent gateways Multi-surface operators: Discord, Mattermost, Feishu, QQ, Google Workspace; plugin & orchestration authors Desktop end-users, strong CJK/heterogeneous-gateway (Volcengine etc.) and localization sensitivity Security-conscious self-hosters, multi-principal / multi-tenant operators, sovereign deployments

IronClaw shows no signal and should be treated as inactive for planning purposes.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — High-velocity, broad surface (OpenClaw). 63.6% PR merge rate with 318 landings/day, but a large share is internal campaign churn ("deslop", batch test removals, lazy-loading). Functionally the most mature; operationally the least stable on Windows and 8–16 GB hosts. Rapidly iterating, release-constrained.

Tier 2 — High engagement, review-bound (QwenPaw, Hermes). Both show the classic mid-scale signature: triage keeps pace, deep fixes do not. QwenPaw converts well-scoped reports fast (#8162 filed Oct 10, fix merged Oct 26; #8270 and #4946 closed this window) but has 3 critical no-fix-PR bugs and a privacy-relevant PR (#7835) unreviewed since Sep 17. Hermes advanced 45 PRs but merged 5, closed a feature request same-day, and has no PR at all for its three largest stability risks (aiohttp crash-loop, webhook cron deadlock, admission cluster). Rapidly iterating on surface area, stabilizing on core. Both have demonstrated maturity signals — production 976 MB history DBs, Docker deployments, daily backup crons.

Tier 3 — Security hardening, backlog rot risk (ZeroClaw). 23 issues in, 0 out; 8 security issues filed in one day with no fix PRs; v0.9.0 work stacked several PRs deep on unmerged parents (#11234/#11230 on #11225). Stabilizing operationally, but accumulating unreviewed risk ahead of a security-themed release.

Dormant (IronClaw).

Cross-cutting maturity read: every project's top-engagement metric is now a trust or reliability thread, not a capability announcement — OpenClaw's 139-comment WAL thread, Hermes' 22-comment session-resume thread, QwenPaw's 12-comment plugin-contract thread, ZeroClaw's context-compression cluster. The category has crossed from "what can it do" to "can I leave it running."

7. Trend Signals

  1. Reliability is now the release gate. Four independent P0 ux-release-blocker clusters held OpenClaw's train; ZeroClaw tags security work release:v0.9.0/release-gate; Hermes' stable v0.22.5 ships with an unresolved session regression. Implication: latency-to-stable is becoming a competitive metric, not just capability.

  2. Session/lease/admission is the new hard problem. Visible in all three gateway-style projects. Concrete guidance: model session state explicitly (owner, lease, TTL, generation), make wakes idempotent, cap retries with a dead-letter path, and make caps reachable — Hermes #143720 shows a _MAX_COMPLETION_* constant that is dead code in the active path.

  3. Compaction must be implemented, removed, or documented — never inert. ZeroClaw's silent no-op config keys (#10781) and destructive trim (#11711), plus QwenPaw's hard compaction failures (#8312), make this the single highest-leverage trust fix in the ecosystem. Ship a token-budget accounting surface, not just a policy.

  4. Silent failure is the #1 cross-project UX complaint (4/4 active projects). Two concrete patterns for agent developers: (a) never return success for a denied, truncated, or dropped operation; (b) make refusals machine-remediable — reason + hint (#11983) — because autonomous agents loop on opaque errors.

  5. Backpressure must be dimensioned by the consuming resource. Four projects independently capped the wrong counter: child count instead of RSS (#161050), thread-pool slots instead of event-loop progress (#145315), default AnyIO limiter instead of task count (#8279), response size after buffering instead of before (#12045).

  6. Cost observability is a purchasing criterion. Quantified waste (20–30% of context on bootstrap re-injection; 21.3M measured cache-write tokens) plus demand for per-runtime thinking levels (ZC #12054) and per-operation model selection for memory writes (QP #7719). Expect token-accounting dashboards to become table stakes.

  7. Strict-spec parsers will fail in the wild. Every project has at least one bug caused by a non-conforming OpenAI-compatible proxy or gateway. Build tolerant stream parsers with terminal-event fallbacks.

  8. Identity and least-privilege are transitioning from optional to release-gated. ZeroClaw's OIDC stack, OpenClaw's pre-exec authorization guard and personal-identity work, and Hermes' HITL bypass fixes all point the same way. Principal-aware tool scoping (not just role checks) looks like a 2027 baseline requirement for self-hosted agents.

  9. Plugin supply chains are an emerging attack surface. Manifest/binary generation mismatch (#11562), plugin-generation capture blocking the gateway (#160959), and an unpinned third-party dashboard script (#12053) are three distinct classes of the same risk. Treat plugin admission as a two-phase commit.

  10. Windows and desktop parity remain an underserved market. OpenClaw's dominant pain surface is Windows storage/update/sleep-resume; QwenPaw is actively investing in deb/AppImage and Wayland portals. For "personal" assistants — where the user's actual machine is the deployment target — treating Windows as a secondary platform is a durable competitive gap.

Bottom line for decision-makers: OpenClaw is the reference implementation and the only project closing faster than it accrues — but it is blocked on a Windows/storage P0 cluster with no assigned owners, and its release readiness is the ecosystem's clearest near-term risk (and opportunity). QwenPaw is the best-managed mid-scale project and the strongest bet for desktop/CJK use cases. Hermes has the richest orchestration surface and the weakest session layer. ZeroClaw is making the correct long-term architectural bet (identity, integrity, sovereignty) but is currently constrained by review throughput. Architecturally, the ecosystem has converged; the differentiator over the next two quarters will be who converts that convergence into trustworthy, bounded, diagnosable always-on behavior first.

Dissatisfaction signals: "zero logs" hangs (#8435), misleading "unexpected error" surfaces (#8276), and lossy edits reported as "Successfully replaced text" (#8415). The complaint is less about missing features than about diagnosability when the agent fails.

8. Backlog Watch

Item Age Why it needs attention
#7835 fix(memory): stop leaking auto-memory-recall payload to channels Open since 2026-09-17, Under Review Privacy/data-exposure issue: synthetic memory traces reach Feishu/QQ and other outbound channels. Highest-priority unreviewed PR in the backlog.
#7719 separate model for ReMeLight memory writes Open since 2026-09-12 Direct cost-control request with no visible maintainer response.
#7874 PawApp SDK/control-plane redesign Open since 2026-09-19, XXXL Architectural PR with no comment activity — risk of bit-rot and contributor attrition.
#8033, #8027, #8034 Open since 2026-09-29 Desktop backend reconciliation, blocking FS work in async handler, inline media body bounds — all small/medium, all stalled.
#8040 embedding reindex incomplete Open since 2026-09-30 Only the "per-item fallback" half was addressed by #8062; the CJK token-budget truncation root cause remains. Recurrence of #5950.
#7912 MCP docs example Open since 2026-09-21 A contributor is offering documentation work; no maintainer green-light yet.
#8178 nested skill dirs Open since 2026-10-11, first-time contributor Needs timely review to retain a new contributor on an XL change.
#8123 Daily Paper truncation failure Open since 2026-10-08 No per-paper retry; whole cron job fails on one bad model output.

Health note: the just-closed #4946 sat open since 2026-06-03 — a reminder that high-severity startup-blocking issues can linger for months. The current 24h PR throughput is healthy, but the review queue (17 open PRs visible, several XL/XXXL) is the real constraint, and #7835 in particular deserves prioritization on privacy grounds.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-27

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw recorded high inbound activity but almost no closure in the last 24 hours: 23 issues were updated (all 23 still open, 0 closed) and 29 PRs were touched (28 open, only 1 merged/closed). The day's activity is dominated by a coordinated security/identity-access sweep — eight issues (#12046–#12053) filed on 2026-10-26 by the same reporter covering gateway auth, OIDC flows, tool scoping, and URL fetching. A second cluster concerns context/token budgeting and memory correctness (#10780, #10781, #11711, #10921), which has been the project's most persistent theme for over a month. No release was published, though v0.8.7 release-candidate prep (#12019 pins translation catalogues to v0.8.7) and v0.9.0-tagged dashboard sign-in work are visibly in flight. Overall the project is healthy on contribution volume but constrained on review/merge throughput, producing a widening open-issue and open-PR backlog.

2. Project Progress

Only 1 of 29 updated PRs was merged/closed in the window, and that PR is not identifiable from the provided top-20 sample; effectively there were no notable feature landings today. What advanced (updated, not merged):

Area PR Status / Signal
Dashboard OIDC sign-in (v0.9.0) #11965 Opt-in [oidc.<alias>] dashboard login; moves dashboard from shared pairing-code operator to real identity
Scoped dashboard chat (v0.9.0) #11986 Stacked on #11965/#11186/#11964; marked needs-author-action
OIDC enrollment correctness #11968 Form-encode Basic credentials per RFC 6749 §2.3.1
Runtime placement docs #11963 Proposes five exception rows ahead of v0.9.0 sign-in/RPC changes
RPC authorization hardening #11289, #11326, #11234, #11230 Stable denial reasons, log-read gating, queued-session ownership, session-data tool withholding — all release-gate/risk:high
Runtime context controls #11910, #12044 Hard max_system_prompt_chars gate; opt-in deferred bootstrap sections
Channels #11847 (XMPP, XL), #12003 (inbound-only email), #11651, #11601 (Telegram 429/transcription)
Plugin integrity #12040 Fix for #11562 manifest/component generation pairing
Web UI #12039 Fix for #12021 stale "unsaved change" highlight
Goal V1 proposals #11880 (3/12), #11882 (5/12) Explicitly draft: "final review: FAIL," not merge requests

3. Community Hot Topics

Issues (comment-ranked; PR comment counts were undefined in the dataset, so PRs are ranked by risk/size/labels):

  1. Context/token economics — the dominant cluster (4 comments each)

    • #10780 — proactive token-budget context compaction removed; keep_recent/collapse_tool_results inert. priority:p1, status:in-progress, risk:high.
    • #10781 — remove or implement inert context_compression.*, history_pruning.keep_recent, collapse_tool_results, keep_tool_context_turns.
    • #11711 — trimming a long conversation permanently deletes older turns from the SQLite session store. Underlying need: operators need predictable, bounded context cost for long-running agents, and they need trimming to be non-destructive. The fact that config keys silently do nothing (#10781) is a trust problem, not just a docs bug.

  2. Transport parity for persisted turns — #10673 (4 comments, P1/S1). Failed/cancelled ACP turns are persisted for session/prompt but not for the daemon RPC path used by ZeroCode's Code pane; remaining slice of #9333. Need: identical reliability guarantees regardless of client/transport.

  3. Long-term memory recall correctness — #10921 (4 comments). Qdrant recall/recall_for_agents pass limit to /points/search without since/until, so time-bounded recall can return fewer results than eligible. Need: time filters must be part of the search, not a post-filter.

  4. Plugin supply-chain integrity — #11562 (3 comments, risk:high, release:v0.8.7). A plugin update publish landing between manifest read and component admission can pair one generation's manifest with another's binary. Fix PR #12040 is open.

  5. Coordination trackers and UX — #11013 (2 comments) unified file intake/resolver/delivery batch tracker after RFC #9488; #12021 (2 comments) web config "Save all" leaves the group save button highlighted.

PRs attracting maintainer/CI attention (by risk & size): #11847 native XMPP + optional OMEMO (size:XL, risk:high); #11986/#11965 OIDC dashboard stack (release:v0.9.0, risk:high, needs-author-action); #11230 and #11234 (size:XL, release-gate, priority:p1); Goal V1 proposals #11882/#11880 (size:XL, drafts).

4. Bugs & Stability

All issues in the window are open; no bug was closed today. Ranked by severity/impact:

Rank Issue Severity Impact Fix status
1 #10673 ACP daemon RPC turns not persisted on failure S1 / P1 Workflow blocked; lost failed-turn history in ZeroCode Code pane No linked fix PR in sample; 4 comments, open since Sep 7
2 #10780 no proactive token-budget compaction S2 / P1 / risk:high Unbounded context growth, cost blowups status:in-progress, no fix PR listed; #12044 adjacent
3 #12051 sop_workshop apply lets scoped principal author SOPs that run with operator authority S2 / security Privilege escalation No fix PR
4 #12046 wildcard tool selector retains principal-unaware tools (cron, schedule, peer messaging, SOP) S2 / security Privilege escalation for non-admin principals Related PRs #11230/#11234 open
5 #12052 limiters key on first X-Forwarded-For entry S2 / security Client behind appending proxy can claim loopback exemption → limiter bypass No fix PR
6 #12045 response bodies buffered whole before size cap (link_enricher, WeChat, multimodal images) S2 / security Memory exhaustion via user/LLM-controlled URLs No fix PR
7 #12050 OIDC callback token page has no browser binding S2 / security Login CSRF No fix PR
8 #12049 32-slot sign-in flow store exhaustible by 4 addresses, loopback included S2 / security Global sign-in denial of service No fix PR
9 #12047 OIDC bearer verification lacks attempt limiter/outbound cap S2 / security Amplified outbound requests to IdP No fix PR
10 #12053 unpinned third-party script on dashboard origin S2 / security Supply-chain XSS on dashboard origin No fix PR
11 #11562 plugin manifest/component generation mismatch S2 / risk:high Runs component under replaced generation's manifest Fix PR #12040 open
12 #11711 history trim permanently deletes older turns S2 Silent data loss in long sessions No fix PR
13 #10921 Qdrant time-bounded recall omits eligible results S2 Degraded recall quality No fix PR
14 #12043 glob_search drops authorized out-of-workspace matches; rejects absolute patterns under read-only roots S2 Tool misreports visibility both ways No fix PR
15 #12021 config save button remains highlighted after Save all S3 UI state confusion Fix PR #12039 open
16 #11825 codex_cli test empties process PATH, breaking parallel cargo test S3 CI/test isolation flake No fix PR

Assessment: the security cluster is unusually dense and appears to be a single reviewer's audit pass (#12046–#12053, all S2, all zero comments, all filed 2026-10-26). Most have no accompanying fix PR yet, which is the main stability risk entering v0.9.0. Only #11562 and #12021 have fixes in flight.

5. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Link Signal
Opt-in external rerank stage for memory recall (/v1/rerank, default off, fail-open to local path) #12022 Memory quality extensibility; low risk, plausible v0.9.x
Honor per-runtime-profile thinking levels for native OpenAI reasoning #12054 Multi-agent, single-provider differentiation; small scope
Validate OIDC redirect_uri against configured dashboard origin instead of Host header #12048 Security enhancement, pairs with #11965 stack
Gitea/Forgejo parity with GitHub forge channel #12041 Self-hosted/sovereign deployment demand
Unified file intake/resolver/projection/delivery (post-RFC #9488 tracker) #11013 Multi-channel file handling architecture
Implement or remove inert context config keys #10781 Cleanup tied to #10780

Prediction for the next versions:

  • v0.8.7 (imminent): plugin admission fix (#11562/#12040), translation catalogue pin (#12019). Low-risk maintenance release.
  • v0.9.0: OIDC dashboard sign-in + scoped dashboard chat (#11965, #11986, #11968, #11963), plus RPC/identity-access hardening (#11289, #11326, #11234, #11230) — all explicitly tagged release:v0.9.0/release-gate. The eight new security issues are likely to be folded into this hardening wave.
  • Post-v0.9.0: a context-management rework addressing #10780/#10781/#11711, and the Goal V1 supervision proposals (#11880/#11882) once their review gates pass — currently marked "FAIL," so not near-term.

6. User Feedback Summary

  • Configuration trust erosion. Users set context_compression.*, history_pruning.keep_recent, collapse_tool_results expecting token savings; nothing happens (#10781). Combined with #10780 and #11711, this is the strongest dissatisfaction signal: features appear present but are inert or destructive.
  • Data-loss anxiety in long sessions. #11711 (trim rewrites the transcript, deleting older turns) is the most user-visible correctness risk for anyone running persistent gateway conversations.
  • Memory quality gaps. #10921 (time-bounded recall omits eligible results) and #12022 (external rerank request) show users pushing memory from "works" toward "predictable and tunable."
  • UI polish matters. #12021 shows small web-dashboard state bugs are noticed and filed promptly (fix PR within a day), suggesting an engaged dashboard user base.
  • Channel reliability. Telegram users hit 429 mishandling (#11651) and terminal voice-transcription retry loops that block the long-poll offset (#11601) — both with fix PRs, but both needs-author-action.
  • Agent self-correction friction. #11983 argues bare "Command not allowed by security policy" messages cause agents to retry variations instead of remediating; the fix adds reason + hint. This is a recurring theme: security refusals must be explainable to the model.
  • External validation. #12042 is an unsolicited Hlido review scoring ZeroClaw 79/100, with a right-of-reply open. Notable as third-party scrutiny of the project's autonomy/safety posture; also a signal that agent-facing review directories are now targeting the project.
  • Contributor experience. #11825 (test mutating process-wide PATH breaking parallel cargo test) is a small but real friction point for contributors.

7. Backlog Watch

Items with the longest open age, highest severity, or explicit blocking labels that need maintainer attention:

Age Item Why it needs attention
50 days #10673 P1/S1 Transport-parity bug open since Sep 7, 4 comments, no fix PR — the oldest unresolved P1 in the window
46 days #10780 P1 status:in-progress since Sep 11 with no implementation PR; blocks #10781 cleanup and #11711 correctness
40 days #10921 Memory recall correctness, 4 comments, no owner visible
37 days #11013 Implementation tracker for accepted RFC #9488; trackers rot without milestone assignment
28 days #11234 and #11230 priority:p1, release-gate, size:XL, stacked on unmerged #11225 — review chain is the bottleneck
27 days #11289 Carries do-not-merge while being priority:p2/risk:high; needs a decision, not just a label
26 days #11326 release-gate fix for scoped principals reading persisted logs — security-relevant and stalled
20/17 days #11601, #11651 Both needs-author-action; Telegram reliability fixes idling
8 days #11847 size:XL XMPP channel — large surface needing reviewer bandwidth before it drifts from master

Process observation: across the sample, 5+ PRs carry needs-author-action and 1 carries do-not-merge, while 0 issues and only 1 PR closed in 24h. The project's health constraint right now is review/merge throughput and author follow-up, not contribution volume — worth flagging in the next maintainer sync, particularly with an 8-issue security audit landing in a single day and v0.9.0 tagged work already stacked several PRs deep.

Data caveats: the dataset lists 20 of 29 updated PRs; the single merged/closed PR is not among them, and PR comment counts were supplied as undefined, so PR "hotness" is inferred from labels (risk, size, release tags) rather than engagement. All issue comment counts are as reported in the sample.
