v0.26.1-nightly.20261025.8e28d5380c

  • feat(managed): session permission rules and Auto approval (#15448) — lets managed sessions declare permission policy up front instead of prompting per tool call.
  • fix(cli): harden serve token handling — tightens how the daemon's auth token is passed and validated.

Note: this is a nightly. The stable v0.26.1 release itself shipped, but downstream publication artifacts (SDK, managed runtime) are still blocked — see Issues #15498 and #15499.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified (38 comments, OPEN) The single most active thread in the repo. A bot-filed, autofix/skip failure that no test can be attributed to, updated daily since Oct 19. Symptom of a deeper problem: the gate cannot localize its own failures, so the issue accumulates comment noise instead of converging.

  2. #13395 — tracking(runtime): Kubernetes tool runtime progress and cross-platform delivery gate (23 comments) The long-running delivery ledger for the K8s tool runtime. Latest update flags two S1 fixes sitting in #15457, not yet merged or ACKed, with six CI failures attributed to that PR. Effectively the release-blocking umbrella for managed runtime.

  3. #15498 — [P1] SDK 0.1.23 publication blocked by integration timeouts (11 comments) @qwen-code/sdk@0.1.23 never published: the Release SDK job was cancelled after roughly six hours stuck in Run SDK Integration Tests. This is the clearest signal that the release pipeline's test budget has outgrown its timeout configuration.

  4. #15499 — [P2] managed runtime v0.26.1 stops at immutable-publication preflight (4 comments) Companion failure to the above: the managed runtime release run passed its release job but halted before publication. Two independent publication gates failing on the same version suggests the fan-out chain lacks a single point of observability.

  5. #15486 — [P1] After auto-compaction, next request double-counts pending tool result + 20K pad (3 comments) A correctness bug with real user impact: compaction can fire while a tool result is still pending, so the next request's size estimate counts it twice plus a 20K pad — ending the turn or forcing max_tokens: 1. High severity relative to its low comment count.

  6. #15542 — [P1] Anthropic provider: JSON side queries 400 on Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 (3 comments) Side queries send tool_choice: {"type":"any"}, which the newer Claude models reject. A clean, reproducible provider-compat break in 0.26.1 that blocks anyone using Anthropic for structured side tasks.

  7. #15526 — [P2] warn mode sends loop reminder once, then 59 identical calls run unguarded (3 comments) Reporter observed 70 byte-identical read_file calls in one session, 59 of them after the single warning. Paired with #15537, which shows the warning can be dropped entirely before model send while telemetry records it as delivered. Strong evidence for the community that loop detection needs enforcement, not just advisories.

  8. #15545 — [P3] feat(context): threshold-triggered handover continuation (5 comments) Proposes writing a handover report at a configurable context fill level and continuing in a fresh context, instead of in-place summarization. Argues auto-compaction causes "silent quality decay" on long autonomous runs — well-articulated and likely to shape the roadmap.

  9. #15567 — [P2] MCP startup failure omits child stderr from diagnostics (4 comments) A missing shebang interpreter surfaces only as "disconnected connection." The actionable error is swallowed. Small fix, outsized developer-experience payoff — MCP setup is a common first-run stumbling block.

  10. #8432 — [P2] Bailian Personal Token Plan model list out of sync; image/video generation fails (6 comments, 1 👍) Open since August and still the only issue in the top set with a reaction. Built-in /auth model catalog for Alibaba ModelStudio drifts from the console, breaking image/video generation. Reflects the maintenance burden of hardcoded provider catalogs.

Also worth watching: #15513 (headless retry classification — currently just "Retrying provider attempt" with no reason or counter), #15552 (catalog snapshot displaces UserPromptSubmit dedup receipt after #14129), and #15527 (post-merge residues from the automation scanner row pool).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15296 — feat(web-shell): allow embedding hosts to pick workspace directories Embedders can supply their own directory picker for the connected daemon via an optional callback, with an abort signal, taking precedence over native selection. Unblocks third-party hosts that need custom FS abstractions.

  2. #15566 — feat(core): durable terminal identity lookup Adds an immutable derived index for completed local activation and inbox records, with the journal staying authoritative and index records rebuildable from validated journal state. Foundational for exactly-once semantics.

  3. #15569 — feat(managed-agent): native journal snapshot storage The PR2 snapshot protocol: a writer publishes a named snapshot of an exact committed head, retries idempotently, and reads verified bounded pages after a writer takeover.

  4. #15394 — fix(managed-agent): pass the pool Harness the Broker pair serve removes The Kubernetes Harness pool now injects QWEN_MANAGED_RUNTIME_BROKER_URL / _TOKEN, matching what qwen serve reads when the flags are absent. Directly addresses a config-wiring gap in the K8s delivery path.

  5. #15564 — feat(managed-agent): preflight Harness compatibility, leftover workers, live service --check gains three first-install/upgrade checks, including building and closing a real HostedHarnessClient after the /capabilities 200 to negotiate exactly as the runtime will.

  6. #15466 — feat(serve): user-scope Skill activation routes PUT /skills/:name/activation plus a batch variant (up to 100 names), mirroring PUT /extensions/activation. Fills a gap where Skills could only be toggled per-workspace.

  7. #15030 — feat(cli): raise workspace skill install limits Splits the transport ceiling from the on-disk ceiling (previously a single 6 MiB / 6 MiB / 2 MiB-per-file / 128-file budget since July). A long-standing practical limit for real-world skill packages.

  8. #15547 — feat(cli): run only diff-related tests in review build-test qwen review build-test now hands vitest related the changed files plus their referrers, for any workspace whose test script is a plain vitest run. Directly attacks review-loop latency.

  9. #15578 — feat(autofix-pr): run unattended watch's fix agent in the background Third part of the /autofix-pr usability series after #15510 and #15548; keeps the session usable while the fix agent works. Notable as the project automates its own maintenance.

  10. #14230 — feat(web-shell): browse managed auto-memory in /memory Adds an "Auto memory" tab listing entries grouped by scope. Complements the memory work landing in core and gives users visibility into what the agent has persisted.

Also merged/closed this window: #15490 (pinned managed extension packages — closed), #15543 (bootstrap sets service account + MySQL with correct owners/modes — closed), #15393 (web-shell workspace directories settings — closed).

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this period.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Context lifecycle beyond compaction. #15545 is the leading edge of a cluster (with #15486, #15552) arguing that in-place summarization silently degrades long autonomous runs. The ask is shifting from "compact better" to "hand off cleanly into a fresh context."
  • Managed-agent / Kubernetes runtime hardening. Issues #13395, #15499 and PRs #15394, #15564, #15569 form a coherent push toward operator-grade deployment: preflight checks, snapshot storage, durable identity, pool wiring.
  • Observability of internal machinery. Requests to surface why the agent retried (#15513), why MCP failed (#15567), and whether a loop warning was actually delivered (#15537) — a consistent theme that diagnostics should be user-facing, not telemetry-only.
  • Ecosystem extensibility. Skill install limits (#15030), user-scope skill activation (#15466), pinned extension packages (#15490), and external context providers (#15541) all point at making Qwen Code a host for third-party capabilities.
  • Embeddability. #15296 and #14230 show sustained investment in Web Shell as something other products embed, not just a UI.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Release fan-out is the weakest link. v0.26.1 shipped, but the SDK and managed runtime did not. Six-hour integration-test runs that get cancelled (#15498), preflight aborts (#15499), and 37–50 minute post-publish fan-out on GitHub-hosted runners (#15465) compound into a release process maintainers visibly don't trust.
  • CI noise is crowding out real work. #14724 (38 comments), #15173, #13009, #13015, #14796, #14104 — a large fraction of open issues are bot-filed main-branch failures, several with "no test identified." Flaky assertions under host contention (#15341, 1/44,637) and Maven Central rate-limiting the shared ecs-qwen pool (#15546) are named root causes.
  • Token accounting after compaction is brittle. #15486 is a P1 correctness bug; the interaction between compaction, pending tool results, and size estimation appears under-specified rather than merely buggy.
  • Provider-specific behavior keeps breaking. Forced tool_choice on newer Anthropic models (#15542) and drifting Bailian model catalogs (#8432) both stem from assumptions baked into the client about provider capabilities.
  • Agent loop guardrails are advisory, not enforced. #15526 and #15537 together describe a guard that fires once, may be silently dropped, and records success regardless — users running long autonomous tasks are the ones who notice.
  • Diagnostics hide the actionable error. MCP child stderr (#15567) and headless provider retries (#15513) both surface generic messages while the useful detail stays in internals.

Generated from github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code activity for 2026-10-26. Comment counts and statuses reflect the snapshot provided.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-26

Issues: 358 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-26 00:37 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-26

1. 今日概览

OpenClaw 正处于高吞吐量的稳定化阶段：过去 24 小时内更新了 358 个 issue 和 500 个 PR，其中 270 个 PR 已合并/关闭、72 个 issue 已关闭，但没有发布新版本。活动量非常高，但主要信号由可靠性工作而非功能迭代速度主导——评论最多的前三个 issue 都是 Gateway 稳定性问题（SQLite WAL 增长、插件捕获阻塞、WAL checkpoint 被阻塞）。项目同时正在推进广泛性能优化专项（steipete 提交的一大批 perf(...) PR），并应对大量 Windows 特有的启动、升级和插件暂存回归。整体健康度可概括为活跃但承压：维护者吞吐量强，但多个未关闭 P0 以及反复出现的 2026.9.x/2026.10.x 回归表明，发布质量是主要风险。

2. 发布

无。 过去 24 小时没有新发布。鉴于已合并/关闭 PR 的数量以及标记为发布阻塞的问题（#143524、#153426、#166634 上的 impact:ux-release-blocker），这一点值得注意，意味着修复正在为未来的版本累积，而不是增量发布。

3. 项目进展

过去 24 小时合并或关闭了 270 个 PR（仍有 230 个开放）。评论最多的集合中可见的关闭与进展：

  • 性能优化专项（steipete）：一系列协同工作，降低各 agent、插件、Gateway、secrets 和 UI 的 CPU 占用与内存分配——例如 #183968（Code Mode 结果序列化）、#183997（Linux CPU 采样）、#184004（数组拷贝消除）、#184001、#183990、#184002、#183991、#183988。
  • 已关闭的性能 PR： #183979（冗余的 PR watcher 源检查）和 #183977（规范投递索引重建）已关闭；#183354（在备份报告中转义终端控制字符）也已关闭。
  • Control UI / 身份： #164825 在设置期间增加配置文件命名（#162164 身份总项目的一部分）；#163765 推进 iOS 聊天中的个人 Tailscale 身份。
  • 正在推进的定向修复： #183964（Gateway 未应用配置时模型设置挂起）、#184005（静默后台 exec 后 Control UI 误报“空响应”）、#183023（CRLF 导致重复回复）、#168510（没有默认工作区的 registerFull 命令）、#179781（已启用的搜索插件未启动）、#177272（Matrix 线程会话播种）、#162918（-- 之后的 PowerShell 补全）。
  • 测试整合： #183985 和 #184006 移除低价值/重复测试——这是在 PR 激增期间管理 CI 成本的迹象。
  • 已关闭 issue： #170332（实时状态数据库变更后 beta 更新仍在继续）和 #83342（运行时别名下重复的 /models 条目）均已关闭。

注意事项： 数据源将“merged/closed”报告为合计数量，因此无法根据这些数据确认确切的合并比例。

4. 社区热点

问题/PR 评论数 信号
#143524 — SQLite WAL 增长到 1.4–2.8 GB，阻塞网关启动（Windows） 136 主要痛点；P0，发布阻塞
#160959 — 网关在捕获大型外部插件时阻塞数分钟 54 2026.9.6 回归，P0
#164294 — 状态数据库 WAL checkpoint 永不完成（被读取器钉住） 33 与 WAL 系列 bug 相关
#168955 — 启动耗时约 1030 秒，而 2026.10.1 约为 410 秒（Windows） 19 升级回归，P1
#159596 — 内存锯齿；prepared-model-catalog worker 触及堆上限 16 每天约 200 次严重内存压力事件
#53408 — 长对话后 Write/exec 参数被静默丢弃 15 最早的高互动 bug（2026 年 3 月）
#67413 — 按 agent 的 dreaming 配置 14 有真实产品需求的功能

底层需求： 评论分布高度集中在 SQLite/WAL 生命周期正确性（#143524 + #164294 + #166634 + #164427 + #164948 均共享 checkpoint/锁定根因）。用户在这里并不是要求新能力——他们需要网关能够启动、保持运行，并且在 Windows 和小型主机上不损坏或膨胀状态数据。第二类集中在 启动/升级可靠性（#160959、#168955、#182476、#183786），表明更新路径本身已成为信任问题。唯一长期存在的行为 bug #53408（工具参数静默丢失）仍是高焦虑项，因为它表现为静默失败，而不是崩溃。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度排序。数据表明存在修复 PR 的地方会注明。

P0 — 严重

  1. #143524 — Agent SQLite WAL 无界增长（观察到 2.8 GB），在 Windows 上阻塞网关启动；wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) 只能暂时缓解。无修复 PR（no-new-fix-pr），需要维护者审查。发布阻塞。
  2. #160959 — 网关事件循环在外部/工作区插件捕获期间阻塞数分钟（2026.9.6 回归）。有源码复现；无修复 PR。
  3. #159596 — 内存锯齿：prepared-model-catalog worker 增长到完整堆上限，每天约 200 次严重压力事件。无修复 PR。
  4. #153426 — MEMORY.md/USER.md 被 provenance ratchet 静默且永久排除在 bootstrap 注入之外；没有诊断或恢复路径。标记为 security-review + release-blocker；无修复 PR。
  5. #166634 — 延迟回收提交 checkpoint 失败导致 agent 在崩溃恢复后永久处于 UNAVAILABLE。发布阻塞；需要复现。

P1 — 高

  1. #168955 — Windows 启动回归：约 1030 秒 vs 约 410 秒；sidecars.control-ui-assets 阻塞 477 秒。无修复 PR。
  2. #182476 — Windows update repair 因 OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST 失败；就绪状态不稳定。需要信息。
  3. #134993 — 2026.8.1 之后，在大型 skill/agent 集群下，网关在文件系统发现中占满一个 CPU 核。需要信息。
  4. #167876 — Talk 咨询在会话建立后丢失调用方权限；已标记 security-review。
  5. #148292 — 会话自动压缩：仅尝试一次、无超时、与主模型耦合 → 挂起 23 分钟。
  6. #164427 — 单次 cron.history-maintenance 扫描持有状态数据库写锁 9.35 秒，耗尽 5 秒 busy timeout 并中止 sidecar 启动。
  7. #177656 — 原生主机 exec 遇到共享状态完整性准入错误（2026.10.5 上 28+ 次失败）。
  8. #181078 — Agent 轮次在回复后失败，报错“Canonical session reader continuation is no longer current”（2026.10.5 Docker）。
  9. #183786 — Windows beta 升级反复查询已停止的前台 Gateway PID；升级停滞超过 15 分钟。
  10. #168456 — 模型回退在 cron agentTurn 的会话转录 turn-key 断言处失败。修复形态明确/可入队（clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear、queueable-fix）。
  11. #126950 — Telegram 不透明 tgcb1: 回调载荷被静默丢弃。关联 PR 已开放。
  12. #149406 — sessions_spawn 子会话遗漏所有第三方 MCP 服务器。
  13. #142116 — 重启恢复卡住 Telegram 通道：300 秒 claim→adoption 停滞，重新派发时没有回复载荷。
  14. #144594 — 会话间消息卡在 interrupted，没有重放或警告。
  15. #89257 — backup create --verify 以 13 退出，留下损坏的 .tmp 归档（data-loss 标签）。无修复 PR。

P2 — 值得注意

  • #164294 — 状态数据库 WAL checkpoint 永不完成（进程内读取器钉住）。
  • #162585 — Windows 插件暂存将自身重新物化到 node_modules，从 290 MB 增长到 612 MB+ 且不收敛。
  • #157986 — 所有 agentTurn 自动化都因 DataCloneError 失败。关联 PR 已开放。
  • #158127 — 多 agent 运行时发布失败 + Codex 启动超时。
  • #112313 — 进入死信的外发队列条目是永久性的；没有 CLI/RPC/TTL 可以清除它们。
  • #164948 — doctor --fix 在状态数据库上自死锁（busyTimeoutMs=0）。
  • #166137 — 出口代理哨兵替换间歇性失效；过期/未替换的凭据到达上游（401s）。
  • #53408 — 15+ 轮后工具参数静默丢失。
  • #165391 — Control UI 会话数与 sessions.list 不一致。
  • #166289 — model.usage 双重触发（相隔 1 毫秒）。
  • #164279 — 后台体验审查完成率 0%（连续 50 次失败）。
  • #138561 — active-memory 插件在 2026.8.2 后停止召回，且没有日志信号。
  • #162448 — Linux 桌面窗口控件与侧边栏重叠。
  • #155600 — 选择评论渲染为原始附件文本。

稳定性解读： 这组 bug 异常集中——SQLite WAL/checkpoint/写锁病理和 Windows 升级/启动路径解释了大多数 P0/P1 项。修复覆盖较弱：大多数 P0 都标记为 no-new-fix-pr。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

活跃功能问题及其可能性信号：

  • #67413 — 按 agent 的 dreaming 配置（14 条评论，5 👍）。防止同时进行工作区 dreaming/OOM。标记为 needs-product-decision → 不太可能进入紧接着的下一个版本。
  • #101422 — 可配置的记忆召回资格和索引排除路径（10 条评论）。needs-product-decision；与 #153426/#138561 的记忆工作高度契合，但未排期。
  • #162164 — 在 iOS/macOS 中选择加入的个人身份，同时保留 Shared owner。正在积极推进：#164825（配置文件命名）和 #163765（Tailscale 身份）已开放。#163765 带有 merge-risk: compatibility 和 security-boundary 标记——很可能分阶段推出，而不是一次性发布。
  • #159858 — 让空闲 worker isolate 释放内存（11–12 个 isolate 常驻约 650 MB）。与 #159596 一致；近期可能作为选择加入项。
  • #55372 — 用于禁用重启哨兵通知的配置选项。范围小，needs-product-decision，长期开放。
  • #140244 — 为 openclaw infer model run 增加 --prompt-file。低风险 CLI 增项；有可能。
  • #130247 — Cron --until / --max-runs 以及累计运行计数器。简单缺口；没有排期信号。
  • #126727 — 原生子 agent 的 provider 感知并发/背压。
  • #165685 — 在 registry-settled 的 yielded collectors 上提供机器可读的 reason。

预测： 下一个版本最可能以稳定性和性能为主导——WAL/checkpoint 修复、Windows 启动/升级加固，以及已合并的 perf(...) 分配/CPU 批次——而不是新功能。身份工作（#162164）是最可能逐步落地的功能，而记忆配置功能（#67413、#101422）仍因产品决策而受阻。

7. 用户反馈摘要

报告的痛点：

  • Windows 上的可靠性是最强烈的抱怨。 启动时间从约 410 秒退化到约 1030 秒（#168955）、升级停滞（#183786）、修复失败并丢失租约（#182476），以及 WAL 膨胀阻塞启动（#143524）。Windows 主机似乎是最薄弱的平台。
  • 静默失败比崩溃更令人担忧。 #53408（工具参数消失）、#153426（记忆文件被永久静默丢弃）、#112313（永久死信行）、#144594（消息卡住且无警告）、#166137（过期凭据）。用户反复强调“没有诊断信息，info 日志级别没有任何信号”。
  • 小型/自托管硬件上的内存压力。 #159596（每天约 200 次严重事件）、#159858（空闲 worker 堆约 650 MB）、#164294 和 #164427（WAL/写锁争用）。用户在受限机器上运行 OpenClaw，并触达上限效应。
  • 2026.9.x → 2026.10.x 之间的回归。 #160959、#181078、#168955、#159596、#158127、#162448 都明确标记为回归；用户正在跟踪确切的构建哈希和 A/B 基线耗时，表明这是成熟的生产使用受众。
  • 积极信号： 高质量复现（source-repro 标签）、详细环境报告，以及用户贡献定向修复 PR（#162918、#166352、#181534、#177272）。社区正在协作诊断，而不是反复空转。

满意度解读： 参与度高且技术性强，但对升级路径回归的耐心明显正在变薄——若干报告已持续数周（#143524 自 2026-09-09 起，已有 136 条评论）仍无修复 PR。

8. 积压关注

横向生态对比

跨项目对比报告——个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态

统计窗口： 2026-10-26 · 项目： OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、IronClaw、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw
数据说明： 计数为来自所提供摘要的 24 小时 GitHub 更新指标，而非绝对社区规模。健康分为分析师按 1–10 分制给出的判断，权重偏向合并吞吐量、发布就绪度、未关闭严重缺陷和审查负载。

1. 生态概览

个人 AI 助手 / Agent 开源生态正分化为大型通用网关平台与更小的专用运行时。五个项目在统计窗口内均未发布任何版本，活动主要由稳定化、安全加固和合并后遗留问题处理主导，而非功能交付。共同竞争前沿已从“新的 Agent 能力”转向运营信任：启动/更新可靠性、状态存储完整性、静默失败防护、多租户隔离，以及本地模型路由正确性。OpenClaw 仍是最大的活动中心，而 Hermes、ZeroClaw、QwenPaw 和 IronClaw 则占据更窄但日益贴近生产形态的细分领域。

2. 活跃度对比

项目 Issue 更新数（24 小时） PR 更新数（24 小时） 发布状态 健康分

Hermes Agent 50；48 个未关闭 / 2 个已关闭 50；40 个未关闭 / 10 个合并-关闭 无；下一次发版可能侧重稳定性 6.5/10——趋于稳定，安全类问题簇未解决
IronClaw 0 7；5 个未关闭 / 2 个已关闭 / 0 个合并 无；仅维护窗口 6.5/10——稳定但人工推进速度低
QwenPaw 6；5 个未关闭 / 1 个已关闭 6；6 个未关闭 / 0 个合并 无；报告中基线为 2.2.2.post1 6.0/10——分诊响应及时，但受审查瓶颈限制
ZeroClaw 6；1 个已关闭 50；49 个未关闭 / 1 个合并-关闭 无；v0.9.0 范围正在组建 5.5/10——高流动、低合并吞吐

解读： OpenClaw 在 Issue 和 PR 更新量上均比同类项目高出一个数量级。Hermes 是第二大活跃面，正处于有意的合并后稳定窗口。ZeroClaw 的 PR 流动量很高，但合并吞吐量非常低。QwenPaw 展现出及时的分诊响应，但审查队列停滞。IronClaw 由自动化驱动，在面向用户的活动上基本沉寂。

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相较同类项目的优势

  • 活跃度和合并吞吐量远超同类： 24 小时内 500 个 PR 更新、270 个合并/关闭，而 Hermes 为 50/10，ZeroClaw 为 50/1，QwenPaw 为 6/0，IronClaw 为 7/0。
  • 平台面最广： 网关、SQLite 状态、插件捕获、Control UI、身份、记忆、iOS/Tailscale、Windows 启动/升级，以及一场协同推进的性能专项。
  • 最强的社区规模信号： 仅 SQLite WAL 这个 Issue 就有 136 条评论；项目展现出高质量复现、source-repro 标签和贡献者修复 PR。
  • 核心参考地位： 同类项目已在从 OpenClaw 及姊妹项目回移修复，进一步巩固其作为参考实现而非小众工具的地位。

技术路线差异

  • OpenClaw 是以网关为中心的通用平台，具有较重的 SQLite/WAL 状态层、插件捕获、Control UI、身份，以及按 Agent 配置的记忆/dreaming 配置。
  • Hermes 更接近统一本地网关 + 桌面端/Web 应用 + profile 多路复用器。
  • ZeroClaw 强调多渠道部署、SOP 范围化自动化和渠道插件。
  • QwenPaw 强调工具层治理、审计日志和提供商兼容性。
  • IronClaw 是Rust/WASM 沙箱与 CI Agent 自动化技术栈。

社区规模对比

  • 按活跃度代理指标，OpenClaw 是最大的社区：Issue 更新量约为 Hermes 的 7 倍，PR 更新量约为 10 倍。
  • Hermes 拥有数据集中最高的单线程参与度——其网关跟踪帖有 220 条评论——表明其用户群信任度高且生产使用密集。
  • ZeroClaw 显示出持续的贡献者兴趣，但审查延迟。
  • QwenPaw 拥有规模更小、技术能力很强的运维者社区，他们会在提交 Issue 前阅读源码。
  • IronClaw 的 GitHub 跟踪器实际上很沉寂，因此无法从 Issue 活动推断社区规模。

注意： OpenClaw 的规模也是其主要风险。多个 P0 问题——SQLite WAL 增长、插件捕获阻塞、内存锯齿、记忆文件被静默排除——仍没有修复 PR，且 Windows 启动/升级回归反复出现。它在广度和吞吐量上领先，但未必在发布质量上领先。

4. 共同技术重点领域

重点领域 体现需求的项目 具体需求
网关/启动/更新可靠性 OpenClaw、Hermes、ZeroClaw OpenClaw：WAL/checkpoint 阻塞启动，Windows 升级卡顿。Hermes：统一网关合并后损坏，hermes update 风险，Windows 首次运行失败。ZeroClaw：fail-open 运行时配置与发布门禁 PR。
静默失败与可观测性 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw OpenClaw：工具参数被静默丢弃，记忆文件被排除且无诊断。Hermes：本地模型被静默路由到 OpenRouter，跨 profile 投递。QwenPaw：审计日志静默停止；有损文件编码却报告成功。ZeroClaw：未知记忆后端静默回退；knowledge_bundles 被忽略。
状态/数据完整性 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw SQLite WAL/checkpoint 与备份验证；大型 state.db 性能；审计 DB 持久性；CRLF/编码保留；记忆后端正确性。
多租户与安全边界 Hermes、ZeroClaw、QwenPaw、OpenClaw Hermes：跨 profile 机器人泄漏、跨安装服务重启、.env 受管目录覆盖。ZeroClaw：范围化日志访问、cron 输出泄漏、SOP 范围/工具名不匹配。QwenPaw：合规审计完整性。OpenClaw：带 security-review 标签的网关与身份问题。
本地/私有模型路由正确性 Hermes、QwenPaw、OpenClaw Hermes：自定义提供商静默穿透到 OpenRouter；基于别名的静默误路由。QwenPaw：提供商拒绝 thinking 参数并破坏 /compact。OpenClaw：模型设置/回退和会话转录断言。
平台一致性与上手体验 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw OpenClaw：Windows WAL、启动、升级、插件暂存。Hermes：Windows 首次运行安装、Linux 桌面端不透明、仅前端安装请求。QwenPaw：Windows 10 文件保真与桌面审批生命周期。
规模化性能 OpenClaw、Hermes、ZeroClaw、QwenPaw OpenClaw：内存锯齿、插件捕获阻塞、分配/CPU 性能专项。Hermes：在 4,583 个会话 / 5.4 GB 状态上重复扫描会话列表。ZeroClaw：JPEG 解码核算。QwenPaw：任务跟踪器清理。
插件/渠道隔离与供应链 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw、IronClaw 子进程/WASM 隔离、审批卡注入防护、图片 URL 溯源、依赖审计、fail-closed 技能扫描、插件暂存清理。

跨领域模式： 生态正收敛于 fail-loud、fail-closed、租户隔离、保留溯源 的 Agent 基础设施。静默降级如今被视为比崩溃更严重的缺陷。

5. 差异化分析

项目 功能重点 目标用户 架构 / 技术姿态
OpenClaw 通用 Agent 网关、Control UI、身份、记忆、插件、Windows 支持、性能 自托管高级用户、生产运维者、广泛平台集成者 单体网关 + SQLite 状态 + 插件捕获 + UI/身份层；平台面最广，但发布风险最高
Hermes Agent 统一网关、桌面端/Web 应用、profile、多机器人渠道、安全加固、本地模型路由 多 profile / 多渠道生产用户、远程 Agent 部署、注重隐私的本地模型用户 整合式本地网关、profile 多路复用器、浏览器 Web 应用，积极从姊妹项目回移修复
IronClaw Rust/WASM 沙箱、异步运行时、CI Agent 自动化、依赖卫生 需要沙箱化工具执行的基础设施团队 以 Rust 为中心、WASM 运行时依赖栈、自动化密集型维护；社区可见度低
QwenPaw 工具治理、审计/合规、Desktop/Feishu 渠道、提供商兼容性、渠道插件 合规敏感型运维者、真实仓库用户、第三方模型用户 基于 AgentScope 的工具层，带防护、审计 DB、渠道插件架构、提供商兼容垫片
ZeroClaw 多渠道助手部署、SOP 范围化自动化、记忆一致性、渠道成熟度 多渠道运营团队、插件/SOP 驱动型部署 渠道插件、记忆后端抽象、接收 capability 的运行时构造函数、堆叠的 v0.9.0 PR

关键区别： OpenClaw 和 Hermes 在网关集成广度上竞争；ZeroClaw 和 QwenPaw 在渠道/运维工作流与治理上竞争；IronClaw 在沙箱化运行时基础设施上竞争。OpenClaw 的优势是生态覆盖面；其风险在于同样的广度会放大阻塞发布的回归。

6. 社区动能与成熟度

活跃度分层

  • 第 1 层——高吞吐平台： OpenClaw。Issue/PR 量和合并吞吐量都非常高，但存在 P0 稳定性和发布阻塞项。
  • 第 2 层——积极稳定化： Hermes。大量贴近生产的反馈、活跃补丁流水线，但存在安全类问题簇且尚无修复 PR。
  • 第 3 层——高流动、低合并： ZeroClaw。50 个 PR 更新但仅 1 个合并/关闭；堆叠 PR 链和审查带宽是硬约束。
  • 第 4 层——分诊响应及时、受审查限制： QwenPaw。同日关闭 bug 并提交修复 PR，但多个开放 PR 无维护者评论，且存在关键数据完整性缺陷。
  • 第 5 层——仅自动化维护： IronClaw。依赖卫生维护活跃；人工 Issue/功能活动实际上缺席。

快速迭代

  • OpenClaw：性能专项加上 Windows/网关可靠性工作。
  • Hermes：统一网关与 Webapp 加固、安全修复、跨项目移植。
  • ZeroClaw：打上 v0.9.0 标签的运行时、渠道和安全 PR。
  • QwenPaw：/steer、DeepSeek Search、渠道插件隔离。

趋于稳定

  • OpenClaw 和 Hermes 都在吸收大型架构变更，处于稳定化阶段而非功能扩张模式。
  • QwenPaw 正在围绕文件编码、审计日志和提供商兼容性稳定正确性。
  • ZeroClaw 正在稳定渠道行为和记忆语义，但受流程约束。
  • IronClaw 稳定但速度低。

成熟度信号： Hermes 明确从 OpenClaw/nanoclaw/opencode 移植修复，OpenClaw 的性能专项，QwenPaw 的源码级 bug 报告，以及 ZeroClaw 的发布门禁标签，都表明生态正在成熟。主要系统性瓶颈是审查带宽，而非 Issue 发现。

7. 趋势信号

  1. 可靠性就是新功能。 所有主要项目在新增能力之前，都会先接受启动、升级和状态完整性的评判。开发者应投入迁移/回滚路径、状态存储健康检查和 Windows 一致性。

  2. 静默失败不可接受。 在 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 中，最具破坏性的报告涉及静默丢弃、静默重路由、静默审计丢失或虚假成功消息。fail-closed 行为和醒目诊断正成为基线要求。

  3. 多租户的到来快于隔离设计。 Hermes 的 profile、ZeroClaw 的作用域 principal 和 QwenPaw 的审计边界表明，用户正把这些系统当作共享基础设施运行。必须显式设计按 profile、按安装、按 principal 的隔离。

  4. 本地/私有模型路由正确性是信任问题。 Hermes 的自定义提供商穿透和 QwenPaw 的提供商参数失败表明，“OpenAI 兼容”并不够。Agent 开发者需要提供商身份、能力协商，并且不能静默回退到云端。

  5. 记忆正在成为控制平面，而非存储。 OpenClaw 的 dreaming/recall/exclusion、ZeroClaw 的记忆一致性与外部 rerank，以及 Hermes 的文档链溯源，都指向对内容策展、相关性排序和可运维性的需求。

  6. 规模化性能正成为差异化因素。 大型状态数据库、会话列表重复扫描、插件捕获阻塞和内存上限如今都是常见的生产报告。轻量级自托管部署仍需要有界内存和可预测 CPU。

  7. 插件/渠道隔离与供应链安全正在加固。 子进程渠道隔离、WASM 运行时、审批卡注入防护、依赖审计和 fail-closed 技能扫描都是活跃工作流。

  8. 生态收敛是真实存在的。 Hermes 正在从 OpenClaw 和姊妹项目回移修复。开发者应设计可移植的基础构件——状态完整性、诊断、租户隔离、路由溯源——而不是项目特定补丁。

对技术决策者的底线结论： OpenClaw 是生态的活动与平台面领导者，但承载着最高的发布质量风险。Hermes 是最强的第二平台，正在稳定一次大型网关/Web 应用整合。ZeroClaw 和 QwenPaw 是聚焦运维者的工具，拥有积极参与的用户，但审查队列受限。IronClaw 是稳定的基础设施细分领域，社区可见度低。在全部五个项目中，制胜路线图都是运营信任优先，功能其次。

Hermes Agent — 项目摘要

3. 项目进展

数据说明：快照报告 24 小时内有 10 个 PR 合并/关闭，但只逐项列出了开放 PR（列出的 20 个全部为 [OPEN]，且其评论数不可用——Comments: undefined）。因此无法逐项归因已合并集合；以下分析覆盖的是管线中正在推进的工作。

合并后跟进工作正在收敛为可交付的修复。

Webapp（#141864）后续跟进——#144741 关闭了 #144704 lane 2 中的四个 “WA-5” 缺口：工作区文件和媒体现在会针对会话自身的 Docker 沙箱或 SSH 工作区解析，文件会保存到其预览读取的位置；该 PR 建立在 #144661 的 SSH-down 处理之上。#144708 修复了 /handoff 聊天在 Desktop 和 Webapp 中跨 profile 类型重新打开的问题。两个相关缺陷被提交而非修复：登录退出传播失效（#144668）和弹窗拦截器失败被静默吞掉（#144673）。

性能与启动——#144640 从 provider-plugin 加载和重启检查中移除了 git 版本遍历，将 hermes sessions list 从 1.45 s 降至 0.44 s（15 个 git 子进程 → 2 个）。#144630 让 sessions optimize-storage 快了 18×（24 m 39 s → 1 m 25 s），并带有分阶段进度。

Agent/工具健壮性——#144745 将工具调用中的退化空白流限制在 4 KiB，并快速重试；#123900 在重复循环时重连流式工具调用，针对观察到的 7–10 分钟 “writing a file…” 冻结。

安全加固——#144738 防止 agent 命令关闭审批卡的代码围栏并注入卡片文本；#130023 将回复图片获取限制为具有工具来源的 URL（关闭一条数据外流通道）；#86189 让后台技能写入扫描 fail-closed。

跨项目对齐——今日 PR 中有相当一部分明确是从姊妹项目移植而来（openclaw、nanoclaw、opencode），例如 #144745、#110440、#144740、#144739、#144738、#131039、#125848。这是成熟度信号：其他地方发现的修复正在被反向传播，而不是被重新发现。

分析。 评论分布异常头重脚轻——一个讨论串（220）的评论数超过其后十九个之和。这种模式是信任事件的典型特征：当 P0 架构变更破坏大量工作流时，用户会集中到单个讨论串，因为碎片化让人感觉有风险。#134889 → #143547 的交接是结构上正确的答案，但 #143547 被标记为 P2，却承载 area/auth、os/windows 和 desktop/connection，这表明接续讨论串相对于其影响范围而言优先级偏低。

#38519 的反应数（31 👍，数据集中最高）是最清晰的单一未满足产品请求，且自 June 3 起一直开放——见 §8。

7. 用户反馈摘要

用户满意之处。 本数据集中没有称赞，但报告的形态表明真实的生产采用：用户引用具体版本戳（v0.22.5+9-g67491b50）、打包构建、5.4 GB 状态数据库、4,583 个会话、5 个并发客户端、一个多路复用器下的四个 Telegram bot 加 Discord。人们正在高强度地使用它。

主要痛点（按用户自己的表述）：

  1. 统一器破坏了各功能面之间的接缝。 #134889/#143547 讨论串描述了 CLI、TUI、Desktop、API server、编辑器、消息 bot、cron、Kanban 和 Group Chats 都把轮次交给一个进程——然后失去各功能面的保证。具体表现：/handoff 聊天在错误客户端中复活（#144708）、活跃会话在重连后缺少 status（#144728）、Bot Mode profile_mismatch 循环（#144716）、profile delete 什么也不做（#144703）、插件覆盖被静默忽略（#144336）。反复出现的词是**“静默地”。**
  2. 多租户正以设计未预料到的方式被使用。 一个 profile 的进度通知泄漏到另一个 profile 的 bot（#143364），以及一个安装的 update 杀掉另一个安装的 dashboard（#141275）。用户正把 Hermes 当作共享基础设施。
  3. 本地模型用户感觉自己被二等对待。 #144437（LAN 模型被静默推到 OpenRouter）和 #140881（alias 重写 model id，静默回退）是同一个抱怨：路由器悄悄选择了一个与我要求不同的后端，而我只能从 400 中才发现。 对隐私敏感的本地部署来说，这是数据集中最尖锐的信任问题。
  4. 上手摩擦存在平台倾斜。 Windows 首次运行安装器失败（#131199）和已存在 145 天的仅前端请求（#38519）；Linux Desktop 在 6% 不透明度下不可用（#143426）。与此同时，macOS 用户报告更微妙的陈旧状态（#144735）。
  5. 规模性能问题正在到来。 #143833 在 4,583 个会话的存储上每次调用重扫 130 ms，是这里首次出现的此类报告——随着用户群成熟，预计会更多。

满意度解读。 中性偏紧张。没有愤怒，没有弃用信号；用户在提交仔细、可复现、预先检查过的报告（其中几个明确列出了他们首先运行的搜索）。这是一个有投入的用户群在一次性吸收大量变动时的行为。

  5. 客户端生命周期 bug（#8416）——来自已取消远程会话的无法关闭模态框。
  6. 上手摩擦（#8418）——“一键部署”与资格审核的现实不符。

4. 社区热点

  1. #8891 — Persistent memory parity tracker · 14 条评论 · 自 2026-07-09 起 open · priority:p2、risk:high、type:tracker、topic:memory 唯一真正有讨论的条目。追踪一个多 PR 推进，覆盖跨会话记忆的 策展、相关性和可运维性层面，根据其自身快照，目前为“7 个具名 open 项：4 个 issue，3 个 PR”。底层需求： 用户希望记忆能像成熟的对等 runtime 一样可预测地运行——不只是存储，还包括选择、排序和管理。这是项目最具战略性的单个 open 线程。

  2. #11853 — npm audit 失败（2026-10-19） · 3 条评论 · bot 提交 · security、risk:high 一个 high/critical 发现，外加一个 moderate 的 @tailwindcss/typography 公告，并关联了一次 Actions 运行。底层需求： 自动化供应链门禁正在报警，且 7 天内无人负责修复。考虑到 Web dashboard 的增长（#11986、#12021），前端依赖卫生比工具噪音所暗示的更重要。

  3. PR 讨论量不可观测（计数为 undefined），因此热度只能从标签和存在时长推断：#11174（30 天，XL，distinguished contributor）、#11209（28 天，needs-author-action）、#11056（34 天，size:XS）。

解读： 社区精力集中在 runtime 语义（memory、capabilities）和 安全 上，而日常渠道工作产生了 PR，却很少有可见对话。六个 issue 中有三个零评论——要么是快速分诊，要么是评审者参与度低。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

按严重程度排序，并附修复 PR 状态：

严重程度 条目 影响 修复 PR？
高 #11853 — npm audit high/critical 构建门禁失败；Web 依赖存在供应链暴露 ❌ 未关联
高 #11209 — 未知 memory.backend 静默构建 MarkdownMemory 持久记忆静默错路由：无法识别的 backend 将跨会话记忆写入 workspace Markdown 文件 ✅ 修复即该 PR 本身，因 needs-author-action 停滞 28 天
高 #11326 — logs/query 和 logs/get 缺少 require_global_stream_access 带作用域的主体可以读取其不应读取的持久化日志 ✅ 修复 PR 已 open，25 天
高 #11644 — cron shell 作业将原始 status/stdout/stderr 转发到渠道 命令文本和 stderr 泄露到投递渠道 ✅ 修复 PR 已 open，16 天，needs-maintainer-review
中 #11283 — SOP scope 组（fs、web）与注册工具名（file_read、web_search）不匹配 SOP 步骤上的 权限作用域不匹配 —— 可能限制不足或过度限制 ✅ 修复 PR 已 open，26 天
中 #11672 — JPEG 准入分配 解码峰值核算；潜在内存压力 ✅ 修复 PR 已 open，14 天
中（静默） #12035 — knowledge_bundles 已验证但运行时从未消费 配置被静默忽略，没有警告；没有崩溃，但运维者意图丢失 ❌ 无
低（S3） #12021 — Web UI 配置保存按钮在 banner 保存后仍保持高亮 在 daemon 重载前显示“1 个未保存更改”；外观/UX 问题 ❌ 无

模式： 这批中最危险的 bug 是 fail-open 或 fail-silent 行为——无法识别的 memory backend、被忽略的 knowledge bundle、未强制执行的日志作用域。今天没有报告崩溃或回归。值得注意的是，一个定义良好的小型 PR（#11056，size:XS）已搁置 34 天，因此延迟并不纯粹是规模问题。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

今日提交的新请求：

  • #12022 —— 记忆召回：选择性启用的 external rerank 阶段。添加 rerank_strategy = "external"，将符合条件的候选池 POST 到运维者配置的 /v1/rerank 端点，并保持其排序；默认关闭，任何错误时 fail-open 到本地路径。 设计上规格明确且低风险——是 v0.9.x memory 发布 的有力候选，因为它直接接入 #8891 的相关性层面。
  • #12035 —— 在 prompt 组装时实际消费 knowledge_bundles（或发出警告）。与其说是功能，不如说是正确性缺口；落地成本低，适合作为 first issue 素材。
  • [#12034](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12034, closed) —— Personal Agent MVP：面向访客的知识与请求子系统。当天关闭，并根据 RFC #5615 披露为 AI。即使在关闭状态下，它也表明意图走向 可部署、面向访客的个人 agent，而非仅面向开发者的 runtime。

预计 v0.9.0 / 近期内容（基于标签与堆叠关系）：

  1. Runtime capability plumbing —— #11174 + 文档 #11980。当前进行中最深层的架构变更。
  2. 作用域化 dashboard chat —— #11986，取决于其三个基础 PR。
  3. 渠道打磨包 —— 可配置的 ack reactions、Telegram/Slack reasoning streaming、Lark 图片、邮件附件。用户可见价值高，大多为 XL 规模。
  4. 插件安装健壮性 —— #11855。
  5. 带 artifact ratchet 的 CLI-only 构建目标 —— #11976，外加 dist-broad 镜像（#11741）。

v0.9.0 中不太可能： external rerank（#12022，全新）、knowledge-bundle 消费（#12035，未分配）以及 npm audit 修复（#11853，无负责人）。

7. 用户反馈摘要

主要痛点：静默错误行为。 今天或近几天有四份独立报告描述系统接受输入后什么也不做——或做了别的事——却不告知用户：knowledge_bundles 验证后被丢弃（#12035）、未知 memory backend 静默写入 Markdown（#11209）、Telegram/Lark 富消息在到达 agent 前被丢弃（#11267）、邮件附件尽管有文档却从未写入 workspace（#11746）。这是数据集中最清晰的跨领域不满主题。

运维者/企业需求浮现：

  • 最小权限强制 —— 带作用域的主体不得读取全局日志（#11326）。
  • 数据外泄防护 —— cron 诊断信息不得进入渠道（#11644）。
  • 供应链保障 —— npm audit 失败会阻塞构建（#11853）。

本地化摩擦： 非英语 locale 同时破坏测试和 UI 行为（#11774、#11770）。贡献者现在正在修复由硬编码英文提示文本导致的测试脆弱性——这是真实非英语使用的迹象。

可见用例： 多渠道助手部署（Slack、Telegram、Matrix、Lark/Feishu、Email、WhatsApp、Web）、SOP 驱动的带作用域自动化、基于插件的扩展，以及——通过已关闭的 RFC——面向访客的个人 agent。满意度信号： 持续的贡献量和细致的文档工作（例如 WhatsApp 语音留言文档，#11056）表明用户有参与度。不满信号： 反复出现的 needs-author-action 标签意味着维护者在等待贡献者，而不是相反——这是流程延迟，不是拒绝。

8. 积压项观察

需要维护者关注的条目，按存在时长排序：

存在时长 条目 重要性
109d #8891 — memory parity tracker priority:p2、risk:high、14 条评论，仍在协调 4 个 issue + 3 个 PR。没有可见的完成标准或燃尽。
34d #11056 — WhatsApp voice-note 文档 size:XS、risk:low、needs-author-action。一个琐碎的文档 PR 卡了一个多月，是最明显的流程异味。
30d #11174 — runtime capability 构造函数 XL、distinguished contributor、release:v0.9.0、risk:high。很可能是发布阻塞项；评审发现缺口（#11980 用于修补文档）。
28d #11209 — 拒绝未知 memory backend needs-author-action，但这关闭了一个静默数据路由 bug。
26d #11267、#11283 Lark 图片丢弃；SOP scope/tool-name 不匹配。两者均为 needs-author-action。
25d #11326 — RPC 日志作用域 priority:p1、release-gate、domain:security。积压项中最高优先级的安全修复。
16d #11644 — cron 泄露 needs-maintainer-review；与安全相关，且卡在评审者处。
14d #11672 — JPEG 投影 needs-maintainer-review。
7d #11853 — npm audit 失败 Bot 提交，risk:high，无 assignee，无修复 PR。无主的自动化安全债务。

评估： 积压项并不缺工作——缺的是 评审决策。两个 needs-maintainer-review 安全 PR 和一个 priority:p1 release-gate PR 正在等待维护者，而五个 needs-author-action PR 正在等待贡献者。清理 #11326 并解除 #11174 的阻塞，将实质性改善安全态势和 v0.9.0 时间线；为 #11853 指派负责人并合并 #11056，将是队列正在流动的低成本信号。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-26

Issues: 358 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-26 00:37 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-26

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw is in a high-throughput stabilization phase: 358 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with 270 PRs merged/closed and 72 issues closed, yet no new release was cut. Activity is very high, but the signal is dominated by reliability work rather than feature velocity — the top three most-commented issues are all gateway stability problems (SQLite WAL growth, plugin capture blocking, and blocked WAL checkpoints). The project is simultaneously running a broad performance-optimization campaign (a large batch of perf(...) PRs from steipete) and fielding a heavy cluster of Windows-specific startup, upgrade, and plugin-staging regressions. Overall health reads as active but under strain: strong maintainer throughput, but multiple open P0s and repeated 2026.9.x/2026.10.x regressions suggest release quality is the primary risk.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24 hours. This is notable given the volume of merged/closed PRs and the number of release-blocker-tagged issues (impact:ux-release-blocker on #143524, #153426, #166634), implying fixes are accumulating toward a future cut rather than shipping incrementally.

3. Project Progress

270 PRs were merged or closed in the last 24 hours (230 remain open). Visible closures and advances in the top-comment set:

  • Performance campaign (steipete): a coordinated series reducing CPU/allocation across agents, plugins, gateway, secrets, and UI — e.g. #183968 (Code Mode result serialization), #183997 (Linux CPU sampling), #184004 (array copy elimination), #184001, #183990, #184002, #183991, #183988.
  • Closed perf PRs: #183979 (redundant PR watcher source checks) and #183977 (canonical delivery index rebuilds) were closed; #183354 (escape terminal controls in backup reports) also closed.
  • Control UI / identity: #164825 adds profile naming during setup (part of the #162164 identity umbrella); #163765 advances personal Tailscale identity in iOS chat.
  • Targeted fixes in flight: #183964 (model setup hangs when Gateway doesn't apply config), #184005 (Control UI false "empty response" after silent background exec), #183023 (CRLF duplicate replies), #168510 (registerFull commands without default workspace), #179781 (enabled search plugin not started), #177272 (Matrix thread session seeding), #162918 (PowerShell completion after --).
  • Test consolidation: #183985 and #184006 remove low-value/duplicated tests — a sign of CI cost management amid the PR surge.
  • Issues closed: #170332 (beta update continuing after live state DB change) and #83342 (duplicate /models entries under runtime alias) both closed.

Caveat: the feed reports "merged/closed" as a combined count, so exact merge ratios cannot be confirmed from this data.

4. Community Hot Topics

Issue/PR Comments Signal
#143524 — SQLite WAL grows to 1.4–2.8 GB, blocks gateway startup (Windows) 136 Dominant pain point; P0, release-blocker
#160959 — Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins 54 2026.9.6 regression, P0
#164294 — State DB WAL checkpoint never completes (pinned by reader) 33 Related to WAL family of bugs
#168955 — Startup ~1030s vs ~410s in 2026.10.1 (Windows) 19 Upgrade regression, P1
#159596 — Memory sawtooth; prepared-model-catalog worker hits heap ceiling 16 ~200 critical memory-pressure events/day
#53408 — Write/exec parameters silently dropped after long conversations 15 Oldest high-engagement bug (March 2026)
#67413 — Per-agent dreaming configuration 14 Feature with real product demand

Underlying needs: the comment distribution is heavily concentrated on SQLite/WAL lifecycle correctness (#143524 + #164294 + #166634 + #164427 + #164948 all share checkpoint/locking root causes). Users are not asking for new capability here — they need the gateway to start, stay up, and not corrupt or bloat state on Windows and small hosts. The second cluster is startup/upgrade reliability (#160959, #168955, #182476, #183786), indicating the update path itself has become a trust issue. The single long-lived behavioral bug #53408 (silent tool-parameter loss) remains a high-anxiety item because it manifests as silent failure, not a crash.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity. Fix PRs noted where the data indicates one exists.

P0 — Critical

  1. #143524 — Agent SQLite WAL grows unbounded (2.8 GB observed), blocks gateway startup on Windows; wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) only temporary. No fix PR (no-new-fix-pr), needs maintainer review. Release blocker.
  2. #160959 — Gateway event loop blocks for minutes during external/workspace plugin capture (2026.9.6 regression). Source repro available; no fix PR.
  3. #159596 — Memory sawtooth: prepared-model-catalog worker grows to full heap ceiling, ~200 critical pressure events/day. No fix PR.
  4. #153426 — MEMORY.md/USER.md silently and permanently excluded from bootstrap injection by provenance ratchet; no diagnostics or recovery path. Tagged security-review + release-blocker; no fix PR.
  5. #166634 — Late reclamation commit checkpoint failure leaves agent permanently UNAVAILABLE after crash recovery. Release-blocker; needs repro.

P1 — High

  1. #168955 — Windows startup regression: ~1030s vs ~410s; sidecars.control-ui-assets blocks 477s. No fix PR.
  2. #182476 — Windows update repair fails with OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST; unstable readiness. Needs info.
  3. #134993 — Gateway pegs one CPU core in filesystem discovery after 2026.8.1 with large skill/agent fleet. Needs info.
  4. #167876 — Talk consultations lose caller authority after session setup; security-review tagged.
  5. #148292 — Session auto-compaction: single attempt, no timeout, coupled to primary model → 23-minute hangs.
  6. #164427 — Single cron.history-maintenance sweep holds state-DB writer lock 9.35s, exhausting 5s busy timeout and aborting sidecar startup.
  7. #177656 — Native host exec hits shared-state integrity-admission error (28+ failures on 2026.10.5).
  8. #181078 — Agent turns fail post-reply with "Canonical session reader continuation is no longer current" (2026.10.5 Docker).
  9. #183786 — Windows beta upgrade repeatedly queries stopped foreground Gateway PID; upgrade stalls >15 min.
  10. #168456 — Model fallback dies on session-transcript turn-key assertion for cron agentTurn. Fix-shaped/queueable (clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, queueable-fix).
  11. #126950 — Telegram opaque tgcb1: callback payloads silently dropped. Linked PR open.
  12. #149406 — sessions_spawn children omit all third-party MCP servers.
  13. #142116 — Restart recovery wedges Telegram lane: 300s claim→adoption stall, re-dispatch without reply payload.
  14. #144594 — Inter-session messages stuck in interrupted with no replay or warning.
  15. #89257 — backup create --verify exits 13, leaves corrupt .tmp archive (data-loss tag). No fix PR.

P2 — Notable

  • #164294 — State DB WAL checkpoint never completes (in-process reader pin).
  • #162585 — Windows plugin staging re-materializes self into node_modules, growing 290 MB → 612 MB+ without converging.
  • #157986 — All agentTurn automations fail with DataCloneError. Linked PR open.
  • #158127 — Multi-agent runtime publication failures + Codex startup timeouts.
  • #112313 — Dead-lettered outbound queue entries are permanent; no CLI/RPC/TTL can clear them.
  • #164948 — doctor --fix self-deadlocks on state DB (busyTimeoutMs=0).
  • #166137 — Egress proxy sentinel substitution intermittently ineffective; stale/unsubstituted credentials reach upstream (401s).
  • #53408 — Silent tool-parameter drops after 15+ turns.
  • #165391 — Control UI session count diverges from sessions.list.
  • #166289 — model.usage double-fires (1 ms apart).
  • #164279 — Background experience review 0% completion (50 consecutive failures).
  • #138561 — Active-memory plugin stops recalling after 2026.8.2 with no log signal.
  • #162448 — Linux desktop window controls overlap sidebar.
  • #155600 — Selection comments render as raw attachment text.

Stability read: the bug set is unusually coherent — SQLite WAL/checkpoint/writer-lock pathology and Windows upgrade/startup path account for most P0/P1 items. Fix coverage is weak: the majority of P0s are tagged no-new-fix-pr.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active feature issues, with likelihood signals:

  • #67413 — Per-agent dreaming configuration (14 comments, 5 👍). Prevents simultaneous workspace dreaming/OOM. Tagged needs-product-decision → unlikely in the immediate next release.
  • #101422 — Configurable memory recall eligibility and index exclusion paths (10 comments). needs-product-decision; strong fit with #153426/#138561 memory work but not scheduled.
  • #162164 — Opt-in personal identity in iOS/macOS while preserving Shared owner. Actively advancing: #164825 (profile naming) and #163765 (Tailscale identity) are open. #163765 carries merge-risk: compatibility and security-boundary flags — phased rollout likely, not a single drop.
  • #159858 — Let idle worker isolates release memory (~650 MB resident across 11–12 isolates). Aligns with #159596; plausible near-term opt-in.
  • #55372 — Config option to disable restart sentinel notification. Small, needs-product-decision, long-open.
  • #140244 — --prompt-file for openclaw infer model run. Low-risk CLI addition; plausible.
  • #130247 — Cron --until / --max-runs and cumulative run counter. Simple gap; no scheduling signal.
  • #126727 — Provider-aware concurrency/backpressure for native subagents.
  • #165685 — Machine-readable reason on registry-settled yielded collectors.

Prediction: the next version is most likely stability- and performance-led — WAL/checkpoint fixes, Windows startup/upgrade hardening, and the merged perf(...) allocation/CPU batch — rather than new features. The identity work (#162164) is the most likely feature to land incrementally, while memory configuration features (#67413, #101422) remain blocked on product decisions.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points reported:

  • Reliability on Windows is the loudest complaint. Startup times degrading from ~410s to ~1030s (#168955), upgrade stalls (#183786), repair failures with lost leases (#182476), and WAL bloat blocking startup (#143524). Windows hosts appear to be the weakest platform.
  • Silent failure is feared more than crashes. #53408 (tool params vanish), #153426 (memory files silently dropped forever), #112313 (permanent dead-letter rows), #144594 (messages stuck with no warning), #166137 (stale credentials). Users repeatedly emphasize "no diagnostics, no signal at info log level."
  • Memory pressure on small/self-hosted hardware. #159596 (~200 critical events/day), #159858 (~650 MB idle worker heap), #164294 and #164427 (WAL/writer-lock contention). Users are running OpenClaw on constrained machines and hitting ceiling effects.
  • Regressions across 2026.9.x → 2026.10.x. #160959, #181078, #168955, #159596, #158127, #162448 all explicitly labeled regressions; users are tracking exact build hashes and A/B baseline timings, indicating a sophisticated, production-usage audience.
  • Positive signals: high-quality reproductions (source-repro tags), detailed environment reports, and users contributing targeted fix PRs (#162918, #166352, #181534, #177272). The community is cooperating on diagnosis rather than churning.

Satisfaction read: engagement is high and technical, but patience with upgrade-path regressions is visibly thinning — several reports span weeks (#143524 since 2026-09-09 with 136 comments) without a fix PR.

8. Backlog Watch

Important items with low fix momentum or long age needing maintainer attention:

  1. #53408 (opened 2026-03-24, 15 comments, 2 👍) — Silent write/exec parameter loss after long conversations. Seven months old, needs-info, no fix PR. High user impact due to silent data/action failure.
  2. #89257 (2026-06-01, P1, data-loss) — backup create --verify leaves corrupt archive. source-repro available yet no fix PR; backup integrity is a trust-critical path.
  3. #51245 (2026-03-20, security) — Telegram slash sessions resolve to channel=(unknown), breaking elevated allowFrom. Linked PR open but unresolved since March.
  4. #55372 (2026-03-26) — Disable restart sentinel notifications. Small surface, needs-product-decision.
  5. #67413 (2026-04-15) — Per-agent dreaming config; 5 👍, needs-product-decision.
  6. #101422 (2026-07-07) — Memory recall eligibility/exclusion paths; needs-maintainer-review + needs-product-decision.
  7. #130247 and #126727 (August) — Cron end conditions and provider backpressure; both needs-product-decision.
  8. #143524 — Despite 136 comments, remains no-new-fix-pr with needs-maintainer-review. This is the single highest-priority backlog risk in the dataset.

Maintainer load signal: clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review appears on the majority of the top-50 issues, and needs-product-decision recurs across feature items — review bandwidth, not issue discovery, appears to be the current bottleneck.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Window: 2026-10-26 · Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw
Data note: Counts are 24-hour GitHub update metrics from the supplied digests, not absolute community size. Health scores are analyst judgments on a 1–10 scale, weighted toward merge throughput, release readiness, open critical defects, and review load.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent OSS landscape is bifurcating into large general-purpose gateway platforms and smaller specialized runtimes. All five projects shipped zero releases in the window, and activity is dominated by stabilization, security hardening, and post-merge fallout rather than feature delivery. The common competitive frontier has shifted from “new agent capability” to operational trust: startup/update reliability, state-store integrity, silent-failure prevention, multi-tenant isolation, and local-model routing correctness. OpenClaw remains the largest activity center, while Hermes, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw, and IronClaw occupy narrower but increasingly production-shaped niches.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues updated (24h) PRs updated (24h) Release status Health score
OpenClaw 358 updated; 72 closed 500 updated; 270 merged/closed; 230 open None; release blockers accumulating 6.0/10 — high throughput, under strain
Hermes Agent 50; 48 open / 2 closed 50; 40 open / 10 merged-closed None; next cut likely stability-focused 6.5/10 — stabilizing, security cluster unresolved
IronClaw 0 7; 5 open / 2 closed / 0 merged None; maintenance-only window 6.5/10 — stable but low human velocity
QwenPaw 6; 5 open / 1 closed 6; 6 open / 0 merged None; 2.2.2.post1 baseline in reports 6.0/10 — responsive triage, review-constrained
ZeroClaw 6; 1 closed 50; 49 open / 1 merged-closed None; v0.9.0 scope being assembled 5.5/10 — high churn, low merge throughput

Readout: OpenClaw is an order of magnitude more active than peers on both issue and PR updates. Hermes is the second-largest active surface and is in a deliberate post-merge stabilization window. ZeroClaw has high PR churn but very low merge throughput. QwenPaw shows responsive triage but a stalled review queue. IronClaw is automation-driven and largely silent on user-facing activity.

3. OpenClaw’s Position

Advantages vs peers

  • Largest activity and merge throughput by far: 500 PR updates and 270 merged/closed in 24h, versus Hermes 50/10, ZeroClaw 50/1, QwenPaw 6/0, IronClaw 7/0.
  • Broadest platform surface: gateway, SQLite state, plugin capture, Control UI, identity, memory, iOS/Tailscale, Windows startup/upgrade, and a coordinated performance campaign.
  • Strongest community-scale signal: the SQLite WAL issue alone has 136 comments; the project shows high-quality reproductions, source-repro tags, and contributor fix PRs.
  • Core-reference position: peers are already back-porting fixes from OpenClaw and sibling projects, reinforcing it as a reference implementation rather than a niche tool.

Technical approach differences

  • OpenClaw is a gateway-centric general-purpose platform with a heavy SQLite/WAL state layer, plugin capture, Control UI, identity, and per-agent memory/dreaming configuration.
  • Hermes is closer to a unified local gateway + desktop/webapp + profile multiplexer.
  • ZeroClaw emphasizes multi-channel deployment, SOP-scoped automation, and channel plugins.
  • QwenPaw emphasizes tool-layer governance, audit logging, and provider compatibility.
  • IronClaw is a Rust/WASM sandbox and CI-agent automation stack.

Community size comparison

  • By activity proxies, OpenClaw is the largest community: ~7× Hermes on issue updates and ~10× on PR updates.
  • Hermes has the highest single-thread engagement in the dataset — 220 comments on its gateway tracker — indicating a high-trust, production-heavy user base.
  • ZeroClaw shows sustained contributor interest but review latency.
  • QwenPaw has a smaller, highly technical operator community that reads source before filing.
  • IronClaw’s GitHub tracker is effectively silent, so community size cannot be inferred from issue activity.

Caveat: OpenClaw’s scale is also its main risk. Multiple P0 issues — SQLite WAL growth, plugin capture blocking, memory sawtooth, silent memory-file exclusion — remain without fix PRs, and Windows startup/upgrade regressions are recurring. It leads on breadth and throughput, not necessarily on release quality.

Key distinction: OpenClaw and Hermes compete on breadth of gateway integration; ZeroClaw and QwenPaw compete on channel/operator workflows and governance; IronClaw competes on sandboxed runtime infrastructure. OpenClaw’s advantage is ecosystem surface; its risk is that the same breadth multiplies release-blocking regressions.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers

  • Tier 1 — high-throughput platform: OpenClaw. Very high issue/PR volume and merge throughput, but P0 stability and release blockers.
  • Tier 2 — active stabilization: Hermes. Large production-shaped feedback, active patch pipeline, but a security-flavored cluster with no fix PRs.
  • Tier 3 — high churn, low merge: ZeroClaw. 50 PR updates but 1 merged/closed; stacked PR chains and review bandwidth are binding constraints.
  • Tier 4 — responsive triage, review-limited: QwenPaw. Same-day bug closure and fix PRs, but multiple open PRs with no maintainer comments and critical data-integrity defects.
  • Tier 5 — automation-only maintenance: IronClaw. Dependency hygiene is active; human issue/feature activity is effectively absent.

Rapidly iterating

  • OpenClaw: performance campaign plus Windows/gateway reliability work.
  • Hermes: unified gateway and Webapp hardening, security fixes, cross-project ports.
  • ZeroClaw: v0.9.0-tagged runtime, channel, and security PRs.
  • QwenPaw: /steer, DeepSeek Search, channel-plugin isolation.

Stabilizing

  • OpenClaw and Hermes are both absorbing large architectural changes and are in stabilization rather than feature-expansion mode.
  • QwenPaw is stabilizing correctness around file encoding, audit logging, and provider compatibility.
  • ZeroClaw is stabilizing channel behavior and memory semantics but is process-constrained.
  • IronClaw is stable but low-velocity.

Maturity signal: Hermes’s explicit porting of fixes from OpenClaw/nanoclaw/opencode, OpenClaw’s performance campaign, QwenPaw’s source-level bug reports, and ZeroClaw’s release-gate labels all indicate a maturing ecosystem. The main systemic bottleneck is review bandwidth, not issue discovery.

7. Trend Signals

  1. Reliability is the new feature. All major projects are judged on startup, upgrade, and state integrity before new capabilities. Developers should invest in migration/rollback paths, state-store health checks, and Windows parity.

  2. Silent failure is unacceptable. Across OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw, the most damaging reports involve silent drops, silent rerouting, silent audit loss, or false success messages. Fail-closed behavior and loud diagnostics are becoming baseline requirements.

  3. Multi-tenancy is arriving faster than isolation design. Hermes profiles, ZeroClaw scoped principals, and QwenPaw audit boundaries show users running these systems as shared infrastructure. Per-profile, per-install, and per-principal isolation must be designed explicitly.

  4. Local/private model routing correctness is a trust issue. Hermes’s custom-provider fallthrough and QwenPaw’s provider-parameter failures show that “OpenAI-compatible” is insufficient. Agent developers need provider identity, capability negotiation, and no silent cloud fallback.

  5. Memory is becoming a control plane, not a store. OpenClaw dreaming/recall/exclusion, ZeroClaw memory parity and external rerank, and Hermes doc-chain provenance all point to demand for curation, relevance ranking, and operability.

  6. Performance at scale is emerging as a differentiator. Large state databases, session-list rescans, plugin capture blocking, and memory ceilings are now common production reports. Lightweight self-hosted deployments still need bounded memory and predictable CPU.

  7. Plugin/channel isolation and supply-chain security are hardening. Subprocess channel isolation, WASM runtimes, approval-card injection prevention, dependency audits, and fail-closed skill scans are all active workstreams.

  8. Ecosystem convergence is real. Hermes is back-porting fixes from OpenClaw and sibling projects. Developers should design portable primitives — state integrity, diagnostics, tenant isolation, routing provenance — rather than project-specific patches.

Bottom line for technical decision-makers: OpenClaw is the ecosystem’s activity and surface-area leader but carries the highest release-quality risk. Hermes is the strongest second platform and is stabilizing a large gateway/webapp consolidation. ZeroClaw and QwenPaw are focused operator tools with engaged users but review-constrained queues. IronClaw is a stable infrastructure niche with low community visibility. Across all five, the winning roadmap is operational trust first, features second.

Where users are happy. Nothing in this dataset is a compliment, but the shape of the reports indicates real production adoption: users cite specific version stamps (v0.22.5+9-g67491b50), packaged builds, 5.4 GB state databases, 4,583 sessions, 5 concurrent clients, four Telegram bots plus Discord under one multiplexer. People are running this hard.

Principal pain points, in the users' own framing:

  1. The unifier broke the seams between surfaces. The #134889/#143547 threads describe CLI, TUI, Desktop, API server, editors, messaging bots, cron, Kanban and Group Chats all handing turns to one process — and then losing per-surface guarantees. Concrete manifestations: /handoff chats resurrecting in the wrong client (#144708), live sessions missing status after reconnect (#144728), Bot Mode profile_mismatch loops (#144716), profile delete doing nothing (#144703), plugin overrides silently ignored (#144336). The recurring word is "silently."
  2. Multi-tenancy is being used in ways the design didn't anticipate. A profile's progress notices leaking to another profile's bot (#143364), and one install's update killing another install's dashboard (#141275). Users are treating Hermes as shared infrastructure.
  3. Local-model users feel second-class. #144437 (LAN model silently pushed to OpenRouter) and #140881 (alias rewrites model id, falls back silently) are the same complaint: the router quietly chooses a different backend than I asked for, and I only find out from a 400. For privacy-sensitive local deployments this is the sharpest trust issue in the dataset.
  4. Onboarding friction is platform-skewed. Windows first-run installer failure (#131199) and the 145-day-old frontend-only request (#38519); Linux Desktop unusable at 6% opacity (#143426). Meanwhile macOS users report subtler staleness (#144735).
  5. Scale performance is arriving. #143833's 130 ms-per-call session rescan on a 4,583-session store is the first report of its kind here — expect more as the user base matures.

Satisfaction read. Neutral-to-strained. No rage, no abandonment signals; users are filing careful, reproducible, pre-flight-checked reports (several explicitly list the searches they ran first). That is the behavior of an invested user base being asked to absorb a lot of churn at once.

No direct user feedback was captured in this window — zero issues, zero comments, zero reactions. This is a genuine data gap rather than evidence of satisfaction.

What can be inferred with appropriate caution:

  • No evident dissatisfaction: no crash reports, regressions, or complaint-style issues surfaced.
  • No evident delight either: no feature requests or discussion threads to gauge engagement.
  • Possible use case signals (from dependency choices only): sandboxed tool execution (WASM runtime), high-concurrency agent workloads (tokio), and CI-integrated agent automation (claude-code-action).

Recommendation: if the project intends GitHub to be a feedback surface, the empty tracker should be treated as a measurement problem. Confirm whether issues are disabled, routed elsewhere, or simply unused — otherwise the digest will keep showing zero user voice.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention, ranked by staleness and consequence:

  1. #7834 — WASM group, 4 updates · opened 2026-08-23, 64 days old · size: L, risk: medium, scope: dependencies The single most overdue item. Long-lived WASM/runtime dependency PRs accumulate conflict risk with every rebase and keep the sandbox stack pinned to older versions. Action: schedule a dedicated review window or split into per-crate PRs to reduce review surface.

  2. #8141 — tokio ecosystem, 5 updates · opened 2026-10-18, 8 days old Patch-level and low risk; should be quick to land and is likely blocked only by review bandwidth.

  3. #8140 — serde_json 1.0.151→1.0.154 · opened 2026-10-18, 8 days old Single-package, low-risk bump lingering longer than expected — a candidate for immediate merge.

  4. #8160 and #8159 · opened 2026-10-25, 1 day old Fresh replacements for the two closed PRs; not yet backlog, but worth watching so they don't inherit the same multi-week latency as #7834.

Process observation: two PR generations for the same dependency groups (#8133→#8159, #8142→#8160) within the window is a churn signal. Reducing Dependabot grouping frequency or enabling auto-merge for patch-level groups would cut review load and shorten the queue.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-10-26

Repository: agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw saw moderate triage activity but zero integration throughput in the last 24 hours: 6 issues updated (5 open, 1 closed), 6 pull requests updated (all still open, 0 merged or closed), and no new releases. One bug (#8416, Desktop approval dialog deadlock) was closed the same day it was reported, and a same-day fix PR (#8419) was opened for the shell self-kill guard regression (#8413) — both strong signals of responsive triage. However, the PR queue is now entirely stalled: the oldest open PR (#8187) is 14 days old and has received no maintainer comments, and all six open PRs show no review activity. The issue mix is dominated by correctness and data-integrity defects — silent audit-log loss, lossy file encoding, and CRLF normalization — rather than cosmetic problems, indicating a maturing user base running QwenPaw against real repos and compliance requirements. Overall health: stable but review-constrained; bug inflow is being acknowledged, not yet absorbed.

Metric Value
Issues updated (24h) 6 (5 open / 1 closed)
PRs updated (24h) 6 (6 open / 0 merged)
New releases 0
Oldest unreviewed PR #8187 — 14 days
Issues with a linked fix PR 1 of 6 (#8413 → #8419)

2. Releases

No new releases in the reporting window. The most recent user-reported baseline in circulation is QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 (pip install, site-packages), with bug reports also pinned to source revision 27d22cd18d6e7fe610536ef1375cebf7aea89215.

3. Project Progress

No PRs were merged or closed today, so no shipped functionality. Work that advanced (updated, not integrated):

  • PR #8419 fix(tools): stop the shell self-kill guard from blocking kill $PID (size/XS) — opened same day as the bug it fixes, narrows _is_dangerous_self_kill so that PID=$(pgrep mydaemon) && kill $PID is no longer rejected. Fixes #8413.
  • PR #8268 fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up (size/M) — addresses the run-cleanup half of #8173, where a hung/cancelled completion callback leaves TaskTracker._runs entries stuck in running forever.
  • PR #8187 feat(channels): extract channels into plugins with subprocess isolation (size/XXXL) — architectural: channel discovery via channel.json without importing platform SDKs, subprocess execution to isolate channel failures.
  • PR #8318 feat(agent): add /steer command for mid-execution guidance (size/M) — Fixes #1775.
  • PR #8314 feat(web_search): add DeepSeek Search provider (size/M, first-time contributor).
  • PR #8418 docs: note eligibility review for AgentScope Platform deployment (size/XS, first-time contributor).

Closed today: Issue #8416 — Desktop approval dialog retry loop.

4. Community Hot Topics

Engagement volume is low and evenly distributed (max 2 comments, 0 👍 across all items), so "hot" here means highest discussion density, not viral attention.

  1. Issue #8413 — 2 comments — self-kill guard false positive. Underlying need: users run QwenPaw as an operator agent on live hosts. Over-broad safety heuristics that pattern-match on substrings (kill + $pid) break the single most common daemon-restart idiom. The need is capability-scoped guardrails (parse the command, don't regex it), not guard removal.

  2. Issue #8412 — 2 comments — governance/audit.db silently stops recording per-agent tool calls despite audit_level: all. Underlying need: real compliance/forensics use. The failure mode is the worst kind — silent, one-way, and per-agent, with tool calls (including file writes) continuing unlogged. Users need an audit-integrity self-check and a loud failure, not best-effort writes.

  3. Issue #8416 — 2 comments, closed same day — Desktop approval dialog cannot be dismissed after the originating turn/session is cancelled (Feishu-channel session, HIGH tool-guard rule). Underlying need: lifecycle coherence between remote channels and the desktop client. Approval prompts outlive their parent turn and become unkillable modal debt.

  4. PR #8419 — linked fix for #8413, opened within 24h by a returning contributor (suantea, also author of #8318). Healthy contributor loop: report → fix → review.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (impact × blast radius × reversibility):

# Severity Issue Status Fix PR
1 Critical (data loss, silent) #8412 — audit_events permanently stops recording per-agent tool calls; rows never resume while the agent keeps acting OPEN ❌ None
2 High (data corruption) #8415 — read_file_safe decodes with errors='ignore', so ISO-8859-1 files lose é/ü; edit_file then writes the lossy snapshot back as UTF-8 and reports "Successfully replaced text" OPEN ❌ None
3 High (hard blocker, provider-specific) #8417 — every /compact returns 400 BadRequest on Volcano Engine AgentPlan glm-5.3-flash: the model rejects thinking.type=disabled, and the compat layer emits both thinking-disable parameters at once OPEN ❌ None
4 High (blocks core workflow) #8413 — self-kill guard rejects kill $PID targeting an unrelated user-started process OPEN ✅ #8419
5 Medium (repo-wide churn) #8414 — edit_file normalizes all \r\n/\r → \n and rewrites the whole file with newline='\n', so a one-line edit reflows every line ending OPEN ❌ None
6 Medium (UI deadlock) #8416 — Desktop approval dialog retries a cancelled request and cannot be dismissed CLOSED n/a

Notable: #8415 documents an unfaithful success report — destructive write plus a "Successful" message. That combination (corruption + false confirmation) is arguably the highest-priority item without a fix in flight. #8414 and #8415 share an identical title although their bodies describe two distinct defects; the titles should be disambiguated to keep search/duplicate detection usable.

Stability positives: #8417's failure was contained — the scroll manager retained the old summary and the keep-context-after-compact-failure plugin preserved session context, so no user data was lost. Error containment worked; the endpoint capability negotiation did not.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

No new feature requests were filed today; roadmap signal comes entirely from open PRs:

  • Mid-turn steering (/steer) — PR #8318 closes a 3-week-old issue (#1775). Fills a genuine control gap: users must currently choose between killing a turn (losing progress) or letting irrelevant work accumulate. High likelihood for next minor release — small/medium scope, clear UX story.
  • Provider expansion: DeepSeek Search — PR #8314. Moves web_search from 2 providers (tavily keyless, anysearch) to 3, adding publication date and authority tier metadata that keyless providers lack. Signals a roadmap toward structured, citation-grade retrieval rather than raw result lists.
  • Channels-as-plugins architecture — PR #8187 (size/XXXL). Reduces host-process SDK imports and isolates channel failures — directly relevant to the #8416 class of bug (channel-sourced approvals destabilizing the Desktop client). This is the highest-leverage roadmap item but also the highest review risk.
  • Provider capability compatibility layer — implicitly requested by #8417. Expect a follow-up feature: per-provider parameter matrices for thinking / reasoning-disable flags instead of a one-size compat shim.
  • Deployment honesty — PR #8418 asks docs to stop implying "one-click deployment" when AgentScope Platform requires an eligibility application with 1–3 business day review.

Predicted next-version contents: self-kill guard fix (#8419), task-tracker cleanup (#8268), /steer (#8318), DeepSeek Search (#8314). #8187 likely slips to a later, dedicated release given its size.

7. User Feedback Summary

Who is reporting: production-grade operators, not casual testers — pip-installed 2.2.2.post1, Windows 10/AMD64, Feishu-channel sessions, Volcano Engine third-party model endpoints, pinned source revisions for source-level bug isolation. Reports are detailed, reproducible, and include root-cause analysis (_is_dangerous_self_kill, read_file_safe, newline='\n'), i.e. users are reading the source before filing.

Core pain points:

  1. Over-aggressive safety heuristics (#8413) — the guard protects against self-termination but blocks legitimate daemon management. Perceived as the agent second-guessing a competent operator.
  2. Silent, unrecoverable state loss (#8412 audit rows; #8415 encoding) — both fail quietly and permanently. Users trust QwenPaw with compliance logs and non-UTF-8 source trees; silent one-way degradation erodes that trust faster than a crash would.
  3. Cross-platform file fidelity (#8414 CRLF, #8415 ISO-8859-1) — the tool layer assumes UTF-8/LF universally, which is wrong for Windows repos and legacy codebases. This is a class of bug, not an incident.
  4. Third-party model compatibility (#8417) — OpenAI-compatible is not sufficient; parameter negotiation fails on stricter endpoints and permanently disables /compact.
  5. Client lifecycle bugs (#8416) — undismissable modal from an already-cancelled remote session.
  6. Onboarding friction (#8418) — "one-click deploy" doesn't match the eligibility-review reality.

Satisfaction signals: #8416 closed same-day; #8413 got a fix PR same-day; compaction failures degrade gracefully with context preserved and explicit fallback plugins. Dissatisfaction signal: contributor LinklyLuck filed three distinct defects (#8413, #8414, #8415) from one testing session — a concentrated negative signal from an engaged power user, and two of the three have no fix in flight.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention, ordered by risk:

  1. PR #8187 — size/XXXL, open 14 days, zero comments. Subprocess-isolated channel plugins. Large architectural PRs decay fastest without early directional feedback; either review or explicitly scope it. ⚠️ Highest-priority review debt.
  2. Issue #8412 — open since 2026-10-24, no fix PR, silent compliance-log failure with permanent per-agent state. This is the most severe open defect in the dataset.
  3. PR #8268 — open 10 days, zero comments. Fixes only the cleanup half of #8173; the hang itself remains unresolved. Needs a decision on whether to land partial.
  4. PR #8314 — open 8 days, first-time contributor, zero comments. Slow first-response on a first-time contributor is a retention risk.
  5. PR #8318 — open 7 days, closes long-standing issue #1775, zero comments.
  6. Issue #8415 — corrupted non-UTF-8 files with a false success message; no fix PR and title collision with #8414 impairs triage.

Data quality note: all PRs report Comments: undefined, and #8414/#8415 carry identical titles for different bugs. Both limit automated triage and should be corrected in tooling / issue metadata.

Digest generated from GitHub activity for the 24-hour window ending 2026-10-26. All counts and links reflect the supplied dataset.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-26

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw saw 56 issue/PR updates in the last 24 hours (6 issues, 50 PRs) but only two state transitions: one issue closed and one PR merged/closed. The remaining 49 open PRs were touched by review, CI, or rebase activity, which points to high churn and low merge throughput rather than active delivery. No releases were cut. Work is concentrated in four streams: the long-running persistent-memory parity tracker (#8891), channel maturity (reactions, streaming, attachment handling), security/runtime hardening, and a cluster of release:v0.9.0-tagged PRs being staged as stacked branches. Overall health: contributor interest is strong, but review bandwidth appears to be the binding constraint — multiple PRs carry needs-author-action or needs-maintainer-review and are 2–5 weeks old.

Data note: PR comment counts were reported as undefined, and the single merged/closed PR is not among the top-20 snapshot, so its content cannot be confirmed. All visible items show 0 👍, so reaction data is not a usable signal today.

2. Releases

None in the last 24 hours. No migration or breaking-change notes to report.

Forward signal: at least six open PRs carry the release:v0.9.0 label (#11174, #11986, #11855, #11976, #11980), indicating v0.9.0 scope is being assembled but is not yet landable.

3. Project Progress

  • Merged/closed PRs today: 1 — not identifiable from the provided top-20 snapshot; the visible top 20 are all OPEN.
  • Closed issue: #12034 — RFC: Personal Agent MVP: visitor-facing knowledge-and-request subsystem, filed and closed the same day with 0 comments. It referenced companion PR #12033 (rfc/personal-agent-mvp). Closure without discussion suggests withdrawal, consolidation, or process rejection rather than a completed decision.

Features and fixes advancing (in review, not merged):

Area Item Substance
Memory #11209 Rejects unknown memory backends instead of silently falling back to Markdown
Runtime #11174 Capability-taking constructors for all turn entry points (XL, 30 days open)
Gateway/Web #11986 Scoped dashboard chat routed through the core; stacked on 3 other PRs
Channels #11754, #11739, #11744 Configurable ack reactions; Telegram reaction withdrawal; reasoning streaming in Telegram/Slack
Channels #11267, #11746 Lark/Feishu image parsing; email inbound attachments persisted to workspace
Security #11326, #11644, #11672, #11283 RPC log-read scoping (p1), cron shell-output leak, JPEG decode projection, SOP scope→tool-name matching
Plugins #11855 Cleans abandoned install staging directories
CI/Infra #11988, #11976, #11741 Semgrep SARIF filtering; CLI-only build ratchet; dist-broad container image
i18n/Tests #11774, #11770 Regional→language locale fallback; locale-independent channel tests

The dominant structural pattern is stacked PR chains (notably from JordanTheJet, e.g. #11986 depending on #11965/#11186/#11964, and #11976 on #11975/#11269/#11973). This raises review cost and is a plausible driver of the low merge count.

4. Community Hot Topics

  1. #8891 — Persistent memory parity tracker · 14 comments · open since 2026-07-09 · priority:p2, risk:high, type:tracker, topic:memory The only genuinely discussed item. Tracks a multi-PR rollout covering curation, relevance, and operability planes for cross-session memory, currently at "7 named open items: 4 issues, 3 PRs" per its own snapshot. Underlying need: users want memory that behaves predictably against mature peer runtimes — not just storage, but selection, ranking, and management. This is the project's single most strategic open thread.

  2. #11853 — npm audit failed (2026-10-19) · 3 comments · bot-filed · security, risk:high One high/critical finding plus a moderate @tailwindcss/typography advisory, with a linked Actions run. Underlying need: automated supply-chain gates are firing and nobody has owned remediation for 7 days. Given the web dashboard's growth (#11986, #12021), front-end dependency hygiene matters more than the tooling noise suggests.

  3. PR discussion volume is not observable (counts undefined), so hotness must be inferred from labels and age: #11174 (30 days, XL, distinguished contributor), #11209 (28 days, needs-author-action), #11056 (34 days, size:XS).

Read: community energy is concentrated in runtime semantics (memory, capabilities) and security, while day-to-day channel work generates PRs but little visible dialogue. Three of six issues have zero comments — either fast triage or low reviewer engagement.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity, with fix-PR status:

Severity Item Impact Fix PR?
High #11853 — npm audit high/critical Build gate failing; supply-chain exposure in web dependencies ❌ None linked
High #11209 — unknown memory.backend silently built MarkdownMemory Silent durable-memory misrouting: unrecognized backend wrote cross-session memory into workspace Markdown files ✅ Fix is the PR itself, stalled 28 days on needs-author-action
High #11326 — logs/query and logs/get lacked require_global_stream_access Scoped principals could read persisted logs they shouldn't ✅ Fix PR open, 25 days
High #11644 — cron shell jobs forwarded raw status/stdout/stderr to channels Command text and stderr leakage into delivery channels ✅ Fix PR open, 16 days, needs-maintainer-review
Medium #11283 — SOP scope groups (fs, web) didn't match registered tool names (file_read, web_search) Permission scope mismatches on SOP steps — potential under- or over-restriction ✅ Fix PR open, 26 days
Medium #11672 — JPEG admission allocation Decode-peak accounting; potential memory pressure ✅ Fix PR open, 14 days
Medium (silent) #12035 — knowledge_bundles validated but never consumed at runtime Config silently ignored, no warning; nothing crashes but operator intent is lost ❌ None
Low (S3) #12021 — Web UI config save button stays highlighted after banner save Says "1 unsaved change" until daemon reload; cosmetic/UX ❌ None

Pattern: the most dangerous bugs in this batch are fail-open or fail-silent behaviors — unrecognized memory backend, ignored knowledge bundles, unenforced log scoping. There are no crashes or regressions reported today. Notably, a well-defined small PR (#11056, size:XS) has sat for 34 days, so latency is not purely a size problem.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

New requests filed today:

  • #12022 — Memory recall: opt-in external rerank stage. Add rerank_strategy = "external" that POSTs the eligible candidate pool to an operator-configured /v1/rerank endpoint and keeps its ordering; default off, fail-open to the local path on any error. Well-specified and low-risk by design — a strong candidate for a v0.9.x memory release, since it plugs directly into the #8891 relevance plane.
  • #12035 — Actually consume knowledge_bundles at prompt-assembly time (or warn). More a correctness gap than a feature; cheap to land, good first-issue material.
  • [#12034](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12034, closed) — Personal Agent MVP: visitor-facing knowledge-and-request subsystem. Closed same-day and AI-disclosed per RFC #5615. Even in closure it signals intent toward deployable, visitor-facing personal agents rather than developer-only runtimes.

Predicted v0.9.0 / near-term contents (from labels and stacking):

  1. Runtime capability plumbing — #11174 + docs #11980. The deepest architectural change in flight.
  2. Scoped dashboard chat — #11986, contingent on its three base PRs.
  3. Channel polish bundle — configurable ack reactions, Telegram/Slack reasoning streaming, Lark images, email attachments. High user-visible value, mostly XL-sized.
  4. Plugin install robustness — #11855.
  5. CLI-only build target with artifact ratchet — #11976, plus the dist-broad image (#11741).

Unlikely in v0.9.0: external rerank (#12022, brand new), knowledge-bundle consumption (#12035, unassigned), and the npm audit remediation (#11853, no owner).

7. User Feedback Summary

Dominant pain point: silent misbehavior. Four separate reports today or near-today describe the system accepting input and doing nothing — or something else — without telling the user: knowledge_bundles validated then dropped (#12035), unknown memory backends silently writing Markdown (#11209), Telegram/Lark rich messages dropped before reaching the agent (#11267), email attachments never written to the workspace despite documentation (#11746). This is the clearest cross-cutting dissatisfaction theme in the dataset.

Operator/enterprise needs surfacing:

  • Least-privilege enforcement — scoped principals must not read global logs (#11326).
  • Data exfiltration prevention — cron diagnostics must not reach channels (#11644).
  • Supply-chain assurance — a failing npm audit blocks builds (#11853).

Localization friction: non-English locales break both tests and UI behavior (#11774, #11770). Contributors are now fixing test brittleness caused by hardcoded English notice text — a sign of real non-English usage.

Use cases visible: multi-channel assistant deployment (Slack, Telegram, Matrix, Lark/Feishu, Email, WhatsApp, Web), SOP-driven scoped automation, plugin-based extension, and — via the closed RFC — visitor-facing personal agents. Satisfaction signal: sustained contribution volume and careful docs work (e.g. WhatsApp voice-note documentation, #11056) indicate engaged users. Dissatisfaction signal: repeated needs-author-action labels mean maintainers are waiting on contributors, not the reverse — process latency, not rejection.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention, sorted by age:

Age Item Why it matters
109d #8891 — memory parity tracker priority:p2, risk:high, 14 comments, still coordinating 4 issues + 3 PRs. No visible completion criteria or burn-down.
34d #11056 — WhatsApp voice-note docs size:XS, risk:low, needs-author-action. A trivial docs PR stuck for over a month is the clearest process smell.
30d #11174 — runtime capability constructors XL, distinguished contributor, release:v0.9.0, risk:high. Likely a release blocker; review found gaps (#11980 exists to patch documentation).
28d #11209 — reject unknown memory backends needs-author-action, but this closes a silent data-routing bug.
26d #11267, #11283 Lark image drops; SOP scope/tool-name mismatch. Both needs-author-action.
25d #11326 — RPC log scoping priority:p1, release-gate, domain:security. Highest-priority security fix in the backlog.
16d #11644 — cron leak needs-maintainer-review; security-relevant and stalled on reviewers.
14d #11672 — JPEG projection needs-maintainer-review.
7d #11853 — npm audit failure Bot-filed, risk:high, no assignee, no fix PR. Automated security debt with no owner.

Assessment: the backlog is not short of work — it is short of review decisions. Two needs-maintainer-review security PRs and one priority:p1 release-gate PR are waiting on maintainers, while five needs-author-action PRs are waiting on contributors. Clearing #11326 and unblocking #11174 would materially improve both security posture and the v0.9.0 timeline; assigning an owner to #11853 and merging #11056 would be low-cost signals that the queue is moving.
